provenance.full_source_extract:
The Matrix is a 1999 science fiction–action film written and directed by the Wachowskis. The first installment in the Matrix film series, it stars Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, Carrie-Anne Moss, Hugo Weaving, and Joe Pantoliano. The film follows a disillusioned computer hacker Neo (Reeves) who discovers that the life he knows is an elaborate deception created by intelligent machines. He is recruited by underground insurgents Morpheus (Fishburne) and Trinity (Moss), to join the rebellion against the machines.
Following the success of the Wachowskis' 1996 film Bound, Warner Bros. gave the directing duo the go-ahead to make The Matrix. The film's action scenes were influenced by anime and martial arts films, particularly fight choreography and wire fu techniques from Hong Kong action cinema. Other influences include Plato's cave, 1990's Telnet hacker communities, and William Gibson's cyberpunk novel Neuromancer. The Matrix popularized terms such as the red pill, as well as a novel visual effect known as "bullet time" in which a character's heightened perception is represented by allowing the action within a shot to progress in slow motion while the camera appears to move through the scene at normal speed.
The Matrix was released in theaters in the United States on March 31, 1999, to widespread critical acclaim. Critics praised its innovative visual effects, action sequences, cinematography, and entertainment value. The film was a box office success, grossing over $460 million on a $63 million budget. It became the highest-grossing Warner Bros. film of 1999 and the fourth-highest-grossing film of that year. The Matrix received Academy Awards for Best Visual Effects, Best Film Editing, Best Sound and Best Sound Effects Editing. It was also the recipient of numerous other accolades, including Best Sound and Best Special Visual Effects at the 53rd British Academy Film Awards. The Wachowskis were awarded Best Director and Best Science Fiction Film at the 26th Saturn Awards.
The Matrix is considered to be among the greatest science fiction films of all time. In 2012, the Library of Congress selected it for preservation in the United States National Film Registry for being "culturally, historically, and aesthetically significant". The film's success led to two sequels by the Wachowskis, The Matrix Reloaded and The Matrix Revolutions, both released in 2003. The Matrix franchise was further expanded through the production of comic books, video games, and an animated anthology film, The Animatrix. The franchise has also inspired books and theories expanding on some of the religious and philosophical ideas alluded to in the films. A fourth film, The Matrix Resurrections, was directed by Lana Wachowski and was released in 2021.

entries.title: The Sopranos
entries.subtitle: Tony Soprano's household and criminal business share the consequences
entries.summary: The Sopranos follows a New Jersey mobster whose panic attacks take him into therapy. Across six seasons, family routines, criminal business and therapy sessions reveal gradual changes in relationships that matter as much as individual dramatic events.
body: David Chase's The Sopranos begins when Tony Soprano, a New Jersey mobster played by James Gandolfini, seeks help for panic attacks. His sessions with psychiatrist Jennifer Melfi, played by Lorraine Bracco, offer another way into the pressures of his family and criminal life. Edie Falco plays his wife, Carmela. The series first aired on HBO in the United States on 10 January 1999.

Tony's household and his criminal crew are closely entangled. Decisions made at home can create problems at work, while money from crime pays for the family's comfort and brings compromises with it. In therapy, Tony's account of these pressures sometimes reveals him and sometimes helps him protect himself. Meals, arguments and routine business allow viewers to get to know the relationships through their everyday habits, so that violence erupts within an increasingly familiar world.

Gandolfini makes Tony's charm difficult to separate from his anger. Chase gives comedy, dreams and uncomfortable silences room to interrupt the crime story, while the ensemble develops lives that extend beyond the boss. Carmela, for example, has to live with the source of her family's security. Over six seasons, gradual changes in these relationships acquire as much weight as individual dramatic events. The series helped make long-form cable drama a major centre of creative work in television.

entries.title: Roberto Benigni: Life Is Beautiful at the Oscars
entries.summary: Roberto Benigni's Life Is Beautiful brought the Italian filmmaker and comedian international recognition. At the Oscars on 21 March 1999, he won Best Actor, while the film received the Foreign Language Film award for Italy.
body:
Roberto Benigni won Best Actor for Life Is Beautiful at the Academy Awards on 21 March 1999. The film also received the Foreign Language Film award for Italy. Released in 1997, this comedy-drama about the Holocaust, which Benigni co-wrote, directed and starred in, brought him international recognition.

His film career began with Berlinguer, I Love You in 1977, which he co-wrote and Giuseppe Bertolucci directed. Tu mi turbi, his directorial debut in 1983, also marked Nicoletta Braschi's acting debut. Before Life Is Beautiful, his work as both actor and director included Nothing Left to Do But Cry, The Little Devil, Johnny Stecchino and The Monster.

Roberto Remigio Benigni ( bə-NEE-nyee, Italian: [roˈbɛrto beˈniɲɲi]; born 27 October 1952) is an Italian actor, comedian, screenwriter, and film director. He gained international recognition for writing, directing, and starring in the Holocaust comedy drama film Life Is Beautiful (1997), for which he received the Academy Awards for Best Actor and Best International Feature Film. Benigni is the first, and only, recipient of an Academy Award for Best Actor for a non-English language performance.
Benigni made his acting debut in 1977's Berlinguer, I Love You, which he also wrote, and which was directed by Giuseppe Bertolucci. Benigni's directorial debut was the 1983 anthology film Tu mi turbi, which was also the acting debut of his wife, Nicoletta Braschi. He continued directing and also starring in the comedic films Nothing Left to Do But Cry (1984), The Little Devil (1988), Johnny Stecchino (1991), The Monster (1994), the award-winning film Life Is Beautiful (1997), Pinocchio (2002, as the title character), and The Tiger and the Snow (2005).
Benigni acted in the Jim Jarmusch films Down by Law (1986), Night on Earth (1991), and Coffee and Cigarettes (2003). He also acted in Federico Fellini's The Voice of the Moon (1990), Blake Edwards' Son of the Pink Panther (1993), Woody Allen's To Rome with Love (2012), and Matteo Garrone's Pinocchio (2019, as Geppetto).

body: The Phantom Menace takes Star Wars back to the Galactic Republic. Jedi Qui-Gon Jinn and his apprentice Obi-Wan Kenobi help Queen Amidala escape the threatened invasion of Naboo. A stop on Tatooine brings them to Anakin Skywalker, a nine-year-old enslaved boy whose unusual connection to the Force places him at the centre of their journey.

George Lucas returns as writer and director in 1999, beginning the prequel trilogy. John Williams’s score adds Duel of the Fates, whose choir accompanies the Jedi duel and gives the new trilogy a distinct musical landmark.

entries.subtitle: An escaped prisoner reopens the story of Harry's family
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban turns a threat to Harry into an investigation of his family's past. Lessons in facing fear run alongside a mystery in which new evidence changes the meaning of familiar people and events.
body: Sirius Black has escaped from Azkaban, and Harry is warned that he may be the prisoner's next target. In the third novel, published in Britain on 8 July 1999, Hogwarts is surrounded by Dementors: guards whose presence fills people with despair. Harry is especially vulnerable to them, reliving memories of his parents' deaths. The new teacher, Remus Lupin, gives practical lessons in defence against dark creatures. As the year develops, the immediate danger becomes entangled with relationships formed by an earlier generation at Hogwarts.

The accounts of the past available to Harry are incomplete, often shaped by loyalty or fear. New evidence changes his understanding of people and incidents he has already encountered, so recognising what happened becomes part of solving the mystery. Lupin's lessons make defence a skill Harry develops through practice; his fame offers little help with the work involved. School life also supplies clues and complications. Permission to visit Hogsmeade, Hermione's crowded timetable and Hagrid's first lessons all become part of the investigation, with apparently small details having consequences much later in the year.

entries.title: Nokia 3310
entries.summary: The Nokia 3310 is a discontinued GSM mobile phone by Nokia.
body:
The Nokia 3310 is a discontinued GSM mobile phone by Nokia. It was announced on 1 September 2000, and released in the fourth quarter of the year, replacing the popular Nokia 3210. It is one of the most successful phones ever made, with 126 million units sold worldwide, and being one of Nokia's most iconic devices. The phone is still widely acclaimed and has gained a cult status due to its reputation for durability and long battery life.

The Nokia 3310 was produced at factories in Finland and Hungary. Several variants of the 3310 have been released, including the Nokia 3315, 3320, 3330, 3350, 3360, 3390 and 3395. The 3315s were produced in South Korea for the Asia-Pacific market.

The phone was succeeded by the Nokia 3410 and Nokia 3510. A new mobile phone based on the 3310 design was launched in 2017; this new Nokia 3310 model comes with a comprehensive update over its predecessor, with a 2.4" color display, a 2 Megapixel rear camera, and a microSD slot.

entries.title: USB flash drive
entries.summary: USB flash drives put rewritable memory and a computer connection into one small object. From 2000, they offered a practical way to carry files between machines, with storage capacity growing from megabytes to terabytes over subsequent generations.
body: USB flash drives entered the market in 2000, combining rewritable flash memory and a USB connector in a device small enough to carry in a pocket. They let people store and back up files, then move them between computers without a separate disk drive or an exposed disc surface to protect. With no moving parts, they offered a durable alternative to floppy disks and CDs. Early models held around eight megabytes; later devices reached capacities measured in terabytes. As capacity grew, the same small object could carry increasingly large collections of documents, becoming a familiar part of everyday computing.

provenance.date_note: The requested work/event and its year correspond to the independently reviewed source passage. Exact day/month should only be added when explicitly documented.
provenance.full_source_extract:
A USB flash drive (also known as a thumb drive or USB stick) is a data storage device that includes flash memory with an integrated USB interface. A typical USB drive is removable, rewritable, and smaller than an optical disc, and usually weighs less than 30 g (1 oz). Since first offered for sale in late 2000, the storage capacities of USB drives have ranged from 8 megabytes   to 1 terabyte (TB). As of 2024, 4 TB flash drives were the largest currently in production. Some allow up to 100,000 write/erase cycles, depending on the exact type of memory chip used, and are thought to physically last between 10 and 100 years under normal circumstances (shelf storage time).
Common uses of USB flash drives are for storage, supplementary back-ups, and transferring of computer files. Compared with floppy disks or CDs, they are smaller, faster, have significantly more capacity, and are more durable due to a lack of moving parts. Additionally, they are less vulnerable to electromagnetic interference than floppy disks, and are unharmed by surface scratches (unlike CDs). However, as with any flash storage, data loss from bit leaking due to prolonged lack of electrical power and the possibility of spontaneous controller failure due to poor manufacturing could make it unsuitable for long-term archiving of data. The ability to retain data is affected by the controller's firmware, internal data redundancy, and error correction algorithms.
Until about 2005, most desktop and laptop computers were supplied with floppy disk drives in addition to USB ports, but floppy disk drives became obsolete after widespread adoption of USB ports and the larger USB drive capacity compared to the "1.44 megabyte" 3.5-inch floppy disk.
USB flash drives use the USB mass storage device class standard, supported natively by modern operating systems such as Windows, Linux, macOS and other Unix-like systems, as well as many BIOS boot ROMs. USB drives with USB 2.0 support can store more data and transfer faster than much larger optical disc drives like CD-RW or DVD-RW drives and can be read by many other systems such as the Xbox One, PlayStation 4, DVD players, automobile entertainment systems, and in a number of handheld devices such as smartphones and tablet computers, though the electronically similar SD card is better suited for those devices, due to their standardized form factor, which allows the card to be housed inside a device without protruding.
A flash drive consists of a small printed circuit board carrying the circuit elements and a USB connector, insulated electrically and protected inside a plastic, metal, or rubberized case, which can be carried in a pocket or on a key chain, for example. Some are equipped with an I/O indication LED that lights up or blinks upon access. The USB connector may be protected by a removable cap or by retracting into the body of the drive, although it is not likely to be damaged if unprotected. Most flash drives use a standard Type-A USB connection allowing connection with a port on a personal computer, but drives for other interfaces also exist (e.g. micro-USB and USB-C ports). USB flash drives draw power from the computer via the USB connection. Some devices combine the functionality of a portable media player with USB flash storage; they require a battery only when used to play music on the go.

entries.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
entries.subtitle: A stolen sword brings two generations of warriors into conflict
entries.summary: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon places love, duty and the desire for freedom within the wuxia tradition of martial-arts adventure. Ang Lee's film lets the movement of its fighters express tensions that their words and discipline often hold back.
body: Released in 2000, Ang Lee's Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon brings love and restraint into the wuxia tradition of martial-arts adventure. Chow Yun-fat and Michelle Yeoh play experienced warriors whose lives are disrupted by a stolen sword and a gifted young woman. Yuen Wo-ping's action choreography gives physical form to relationships shaped by duty and feelings that remain unspoken.

Li Mu Bai plans to leave his fighting life behind, until the theft of Green Destiny draws him back. Yu Shu Lien's investigation leads her towards Jen, a young aristocrat facing an arranged marriage. The older warriors have learned to contain their desires, while Jen resists the future chosen for her. Their encounters bring these different ideas of freedom and responsibility into the fights themselves. Jen's skill gives her ways to escape, leaving her to decide how she wants to live.

Each setting changes the action. Pursuits carry the fighters across city rooftops; a succession of weapons tests their control and ability to adapt; a confrontation in a bamboo forest takes on an almost weightless rhythm. Their techniques make differences of character visible through movement. Tan Dun's score, with cello performed by Yo-Yo Ma, adds to the adventure's sense of longing. The film won four Academy Awards, including Foreign Language Film.

entries.subtitle: An international tournament puts Harry under public scrutiny
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire draws Harry into an international competition he is too young to enter. Dangerous tasks and public attention complicate friendships, while the story opens Hogwarts to a wider magical world.
body: Harry is too young to enter the Triwizard Tournament, yet the enchanted cup names him as a competitor. He must prepare for dangerous tasks alongside older champions from Hogwarts and two visiting schools, relying on his friends while trying to discover who put his name into the cup. J.K. Rowling's fourth novel was published on 8 July 2000, when Bloomsbury and Scholastic released it on the same day in Britain and the United States.

The Quidditch World Cup and the visiting schools expand the magical world beyond Harry's familiar classrooms and rivalries. The tournament brings him public attention, and newspapers turn private events into stories he cannot control. Under that scrutiny, friendship becomes harder to manage. Ron's jealousy and the awkwardness of the Yule Ball belong to the same year as the competition's dangerous tasks. As the tournament progresses, its formal rules and celebrations are accompanied by increasingly troubling signs of a threat extending beyond Hogwarts.

entries.title: Discovery
entries.summary: Discovery is the second studio album by the French electronic music duo Daft Punk, released on 12 March 2001 by Virgin Records.
body:
Discovery is the second studio album by the French electronic music duo Daft Punk, released on 12 March 2001 by Virgin Records. It moved from the Chicago house of their first album, Homework (1997), to a house style inspired by disco, post-disco, garage house, and R&B. Thomas Bangalter of Daft Punk described Discovery as an exploration of song structures, musical forms, and childhood nostalgia, compared to the "raw" electronic music of Homework.

Discovery was recorded at Bangalter's home in Paris between 1998 and 2000. It features extensive sampling; some samples are from older records, while others were created by Daft Punk. The electronic musicians Romanthony, Todd Edwards, and DJ Sneak collaborated on some tracks. For the music videos, Daft Punk developed a concept that merged science fiction with the entertainment industry. Inspired by their childhood love for Japanese anime, the duo collaborated with Leiji Matsumoto to produce Interstella 5555: The 5tory of the 5ecret 5tar 5ystem, an anime film with Discovery as the soundtrack.

entries.title: iPod
entries.summary: The iPod is a discontinued series of portable media players and multi-purpose mobile devices that were designed and marketed by Apple from 2001 to 2022.
body:
The iPod is a discontinued series of portable media players and multi-purpose mobile devices that were designed and marketed by Apple from 2001 to 2022. The first version was released on November 10, 2001, 10 months after the Macintosh version of iTunes was released. Apple has sold an estimated 450 million iPods. Apple officially discontinued the iPod product line on May 10, 2022. The iPod is the longest-running product discontinued by Apple, with a total lifespan of over 20 years.

Some versions of the iPod can serve as external data storage devices, like other digital music players. Prior to macOS 10.15, Apple's iTunes software (and other alternative software) could be used to transfer music, photos, videos, games, contact information, e-mail settings, Web bookmarks, and calendars to the devices supporting these features from computers using certain versions of Apple macOS and Microsoft Windows operating systems.

entries.title: Spirited Away
entries.summary: Spirited Away follows Chihiro, a young girl who works in a spirit world's bathhouse to help her transformed parents. Hayao Miyazaki developed the animated film with a friend's ten-year-old daughter in mind.
body: Hayao Miyazaki's Spirited Away opened in Japan on 20 July 2001. After her parents become pigs, Chihiro takes a job in a witch's bathhouse while looking for a way to free them and return home. This spirit world draws on the kami of Japanese Shinto tradition. Miyazaki developed the story with a friend's ten-year-old daughter in mind, placing a girl of that age at its centre. Studio Ghibli began production in 2000, with Toshio Suzuki producing the animated film.

provenance.full_source_extract:
Spirited Away is a 2001 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki. It was produced by Toshio Suzuki, animated by Studio Ghibli, and distributed by Toho. The film stars Rumi Hiiragi, alongside Miyu Irino, Mari Natsuki, Takashi Naito, Yasuko Sawaguchi, Tsunehiko Kamijō, Takehiko Ono, and Bunta Sugawara. It follows a young girl named  Chihiro "Sen" Ogino, who moves to a new neighborhood and inadvertently enters the world of kami (spirits of Japanese Shinto folklore). After her parents are turned into pigs by the witch Yubaba, Chihiro takes a job working in Yubaba's bathhouse to find a way to free herself and her parents and return to the human world.
Miyazaki wrote the screenplay after he decided the film would be based on the ten-year-old daughter of his friend Seiji Okuda, the film's associate producer, who came to visit his house each summer. At the time, Miyazaki was developing two personal projects, but they were rejected. With a budget of US$19 million, production of Spirited Away began in 2000. Pixar animator John Lasseter, a fan and friend of Miyazaki, convinced Walt Disney Studios  to buy the film's North American distribution rights, and served as executive producer of its English-dubbed version. Lasseter then hired Kirk Wise as director and Donald W. Ernst as producer, while screenwriters Cindy and Donald Hewitt wrote the English-language dialogue to match the characters' original Japanese-language lip movements.
Released in Japan on 20 July 2001, Spirited Away was universally acclaimed and commercially successful, grossing US$396 million at the worldwide box office. It became the highest-grossing film in Japanese history with a total of ¥31.68 billion. It held the record for 19 years until it was surpassed by Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Mugen Train in 2020.
Spirited Away was a co-recipient of the Golden Bear at the 2002 Berlin International Film Festival and became the first hand-drawn, non-English-language animated film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 75th Academy Awards. The film is frequently regarded as one of the greatest films ever made, placing #75 on Sight and Sound's "100 Greatest Films of All Time" poll in 2022.

entries.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
entries.summary: The Fellowship of the Ring begins Peter Jackson's film adaptation of Tolkien with a journey towards Mordor. Frodo and eight companions carry the conflict across Middle-earth into the dangers and loyalties of a travelling group.
body: Peter Jackson's The Fellowship of the Ring opened his film trilogy in American cinemas on 19 December 2001. Adapted from Tolkien by Jackson, Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens, it follows Frodo Baggins after he comes into possession of the One Ring. Sauron wants its power, and destroying it requires a journey to Mount Doom in Mordor. Eight companions join Frodo to form the Fellowship. Through their travels, a vast conflict takes on the perspective of a small group. Elijah Wood as Frodo and Ian McKellen as Gandalf are part of the ensemble bringing Middle-earth's peoples and loyalties to the screen.

provenance.full_source_extract:
The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2001 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson from a screenplay by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, and Jackson. It is based on J. R. R. Tolkien's 1954 The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of the novel The Lord of the Rings. The film is the first instalment in the Lord of the Rings trilogy. It features an ensemble cast including Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Liv Tyler, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Cate Blanchett, John Rhys-Davies, Billy Boyd, Dominic Monaghan in his film debut, Orlando Bloom, Christopher Lee, Hugo Weaving, Sean Bean, Ian Holm, and Andy Serkis.
Set in Middle-earth, the story tells of the Dark Lord Sauron, who seeks the One Ring, which contains part of his might, to return to power. The Ring has found its way to the young hobbit Frodo Baggins. The fate of Middle-earth hangs in the balance as Frodo and eight companions (who form the eponymous Fellowship of the Ring) begin their perilous journey to Mount Doom in the land of Mordor, the only place where the Ring can be destroyed. The Fellowship of the Ring was financed and distributed by American studio New Line Cinema, but filmed and edited entirely in Jackson's native New Zealand, concurrently with the other two parts of the trilogy.
It premiered on 10 December 2001 at the Odeon Leicester Square in London and was released on 19 December in the United States and on 20 December in New Zealand. The film was acclaimed by critics and audiences, who considered it a landmark in filmmaking and an achievement in the fantasy film genre, with praise for the visual effects, performances, direction, screenplay, musical score, and faithfulness to the source material. It grossed $868 million worldwide during its original theatrical run, making it the second-highest-grossing film of 2001 and the fifth-highest-grossing film of all time at the time of its release. Following subsequent reissues, it has grossed $897 million. Like its successors, The Fellowship of the Ring is widely recognised as one of the greatest and most influential films ever made. The film received numerous accolades; at the 74th Academy Awards, it was nominated for thirteen awards, including Best Picture, winning for Best Cinematography, Best Makeup, Best Original Score, and Best Visual Effects.
In 2007, the American Film Institute named it one of the 100 greatest American films in history, being both the most recent film and the only film released in the 21st century to make it to the list. In 2021, the film was selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant". Two sequels, The Two Towers and The Return of the King, followed in 2002 and 2003, respectively.

entries.title: Wikipedia
entries.summary: Wikipedia is a free online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteer editors, known as Wikipedians, through open collaboration and the wiki software MediaWiki.
body:
Wikipedia is a free online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteer editors, known as Wikipedians, through open collaboration and the wiki software MediaWiki. Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, Wikipedia has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit organization funded mainly by donations from readers. Wikipedia is the largest and most read reference work in history.

Initially available only in English, Wikipedia has grown to over 300 languages and is one of the world's most visited websites as of 2026. The English Wikipedia, with over 7 million articles, remains the largest of the editions, which together comprise more than 68 million articles and attract more than 1.5 billion unique device visits and 13 million edits per month (about five edits per second on average)  as of April 2024. As of December 2025, over 25% of Wikipedia's traffic comes from the United States, while Japan accounts for nearly 7%, and the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia each represent around 5%.

Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, Wikipedia has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit organization funded mainly by donations from readers. Wikipedia is the largest and most read reference work in history.
Initially available only in English, Wikipedia has grown to over 300 languages and is one of the world's most visited websites as of 2026. The English Wikipedia, with over 7 million articles, remains the largest of the editions, which together comprise more than 68 million articles and attract more than 1.5 billion unique device visits and 13 million edits per month (about five edits per second on average)  as of April 2024. As of December 2025, over 25% of Wikipedia's traffic comes from the United States, while Japan accounts for nearly 7%, and the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia each represent around 5%.
Wikipedia has been praised for its internal structure and culture, enabling the democratization of knowledge, and for its extensive coverage on various topics. The encyclopedia has also been criticized for systemic bias, such as a gender bias against women and a geographical bias against the Global South. The reliability of Wikipedia was frequently criticized in the 2000s, but has received greater praise from the late 2010s onward. Censorship of Wikipedia by national governments has ranged from censoring specific pages to the entire site, sometimes due to its criticism of the government, or for content considered blasphemous. Wikipedia articles on breaking news are accessed as sources for up-to-date information by many.

entries.title: Amélie
entries.subtitle: Small surprises change lives in Montmartre
entries.summary: Amélie is a romantic comedy about an imaginative Montmartre waitress who quietly intervenes in other people's lives. Jean-Pierre Jeunet gives objects, habits and carefully arranged encounters a central role in a story that eventually asks her to take part herself.
body: In Jean-Pierre Jeunet's Amélie, a young waitress in Montmartre begins arranging small surprises for the people around her. Audrey Tautou plays Amélie Poulain, whose vivid imagination accompanies a reluctance to reveal her own feelings. Released in France on 25 April 2001, the film develops its romantic comedy through a carefully composed picture of everyday pleasures.

A hidden box of childhood keepsakes gives Amélie her first task: returning it to its former owner without letting him know who found it. His response encourages her to intervene elsewhere in the neighbourhood. Objects, notes and precisely timed meetings set her plans in motion, with Jeunet arranging the steps like small mechanisms. When she becomes interested in Nino, a collector of discarded photo-booth pictures, these skills bring her to a different problem. Helping others find happiness has allowed her to stay out of view; now she must risk becoming involved herself.

Strong reds and greens, detailed interiors and sudden flights of imagination shape the film's Paris. Lists of private likes and dislikes give even minor characters a distinct presence, while Yann Tiersen's music connects their separate routines. The romance draws much of its charm from this attention to small habits. At the 2002 Césars, Amélie won Best Film and Best Director, with further awards for Tiersen's original music and Aline Bonetto's production design.

entries.subtitle: A second park takes shape around maritime journeys
entries.summary: Tokyo DisneySea opened beside Tokyo Disneyland as a separate park built around the sea. Imagined ports and maritime journeys gave Oriental Land and Disney a new setting, developed through years of discussion between their Japanese and American teams.
body: Tokyo DisneySea opened its gates at 8 a.m. on 4 September 2001, with an inauguration at Mediterranean Harbor. Oriental Land and Disney had built the resort's second park around maritime journeys and imagined ports. Plans for another park were announced in 1988; the sea-based concept took shape in 1992, and the DisneySea name was made public in 1997. Discussions between the Japanese and American partners also produced the entrance AquaSphere, which presents Earth as a water planet. The opening gave the resort a second, distinct park alongside Tokyo Disneyland.

entries.title: September 11 attacks
entries.summary: The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001.
body:
The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001. A total of 19 hijackers commandeered four commercial passenger airliners. The first two planes were flown into each of the Twin Towers at the World Trade Center in New York City, while the third plane crashed into the Pentagon, the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense, in Arlington County, Virginia. The fourth plane crashed in a rural field in Pennsylvania during a passenger revolt.

The attacks killed 2,977 people, injured thousands more, and gave rise to long-term health consequences while causing at least US$10 billion in infrastructure and property damage.

provenance.full_source_extract:
The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001. A total of 19 hijackers commandeered four commercial passenger airliners. The first two planes were flown into each of the Twin Towers at the World Trade Center in New York City, while the third plane crashed into the Pentagon, the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense, in Arlington County, Virginia. The fourth plane crashed in a rural field in Pennsylvania during a passenger revolt.
The ringleader, Mohamed Atta, flew American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower of the World Trade Center at 8:46 a.m. At 9:03 a.m. Marwan al-Shehhi flew United Airlines Flight 175 into the South Tower. Both collapsed within an hour and forty-two minutes, destroying the remaining five structures in the complex. Hani Hanjour flew American Airlines Flight 77 into the Pentagon at 9:37 a.m., causing a partial collapse. United Airlines Flight 93, hijacked by Ziad Jarrah, was believed to target either the United States Capitol or the White House. Alerted to the previous attacks, the passengers revolted and the hijackers crashed the aircraft into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, at 10:03 a.m. The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a ground stop for all traffic in U.S. airspace, requiring all airborne aircraft to return to their point of origin or divert to Canada. The actions undertaken in Canada to support incoming aircraft and their occupants were collectively titled Operation Yellow Ribbon.
That evening, the Central Intelligence Agency informed President George W. Bush that its Counterterrorism Center had identified the attacks as having been the work of al-Qaeda under Osama bin Laden. The United States responded by invading Afghanistan and launching its Global War on Terror, with the stated goal of eliminating hostile groups it deemed terrorist organizations and the governments the United States identified as supporting them. NATO's invocation of Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty—its only usage to date—called upon allies to fight al-Qaeda as well. As U.S. and allied invasion forces swept through Afghanistan, bin Laden eluded them. He denied any involvement until 2004, when excerpts of a taped statement in which he accepted responsibility for the attacks were released. Al-Qaeda's cited motivations included U.S. support of Israel, the presence of U.S. military bases in Saudi Arabia, and sanctions against Iraq. The nearly decade-long manhunt for bin Laden concluded in May 2011, when he was killed during a U.S. military raid in Abbottabad, Pakistan. The war in Afghanistan continued for another decade.
The attacks killed 2,977 people, injured thousands more, and gave rise to long-term health consequences while causing at least US$10 billion in infrastructure and property damage. It remains the deadliest terrorist attack in history, as well as the deadliest incident for firefighters and law enforcement personnel in American history, killing 343 and 72 members, respectively. The crashes of Flight 11 and Flight 175 were the deadliest aviation disasters of all time, and the collision of Flight 77 with the Pentagon resulted in the fourth-highest number of ground fatalities in a plane crash in history. The destruction of the World Trade Center and its environs seriously harmed the U.S. economy and induced global market shocks. Many other countries tightened airport security, strengthened anti-terrorism legislation and expanded their powers of law enforcement and intelligence agencies. The total number of deaths caused by the attacks, combined with the death tolls from the conflicts they directly triggered, has been estimated by the Costs of War Project to be more than 4.5 million.
Cleanup of the World Trade Center site (colloquially known as "Ground Zero") was completed in May 2002, while the Pentagon was repaired within a year. After delays in the design of a replacement complex, six new buildings were planned to replace the lost towers at the World Trade Center site, along with a museum and memorial dedicated to those who were killed or injured in the attacks. The tallest building, One World Trade Center, began construction in 2006 and opened in 2014. Memorials to the attacks include the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York City; the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington County, Virginia; and the Flight 93 National Memorial at the Pennsylvania crash site.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
entries.subtitle: Chris Columbus brings Hogwarts to the cinema
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone takes Harry from his relatives' home into the everyday life of a school for magic. Chris Columbus's film makes friendship, discovery and recurring places the foundations of a new cinema series.
body: A letter gives Harry Potter a way beyond the home of the relatives who have raised him. His journey to Hogwarts reveals a hidden shopping street, a railway platform and a school where magic fills the timetable. Chris Columbus casts Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint and Emma Watson as Harry, Ron and Hermione. Their friendship leads into the mystery of a protected object inside the castle. The film opened in Britain and the United States on 16 November 2001, following its London premiere on 4 November.

The first film established settings that later instalments could revisit. Built in 2000, the Great Hall gave the young actors a physical space for feasts, lessons and ceremonies, with visual effects completing its enchanted ceiling. John Williams's music, especially Hedwig's Theme, also carries the journey from the Dursleys' house into the larger world. Steve Kloves adapted Rowling's novel around the progression of the school year: arrival and discovery gradually lead to a challenge in which each friend's abilities have a part to play.

Building places the series could return to

entries.title: Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones
entries.summary: Anakin protects Senator Padmé Amidala while Obi-Wan investigates an assassination attempt. Their separate paths lead into the crisis that begins the Clone Wars.
story_headings: Protecting Padmé as war approaches
A romance within the Republic’s crisis
body: Attack of the Clones takes place ten years after Naboo’s invasion. Padmé Amidala, now a senator, survives an assassination attempt and receives protection from the Jedi apprentice Anakin Skywalker. While their relationship develops, Obi-Wan Kenobi investigates the attack. His search leads toward a hidden army as Count Dooku’s Separatists threaten to leave the Republic.

George Lucas’s 2002 film connects Anakin and Padmé’s growing attachment with a political conflict moving toward open war. Across the Stars, John Williams’s love theme, gives that relationship its musical thread. The investigation and the romance eventually draw the protagonists into the same crisis, opening the Clone Wars that shape the following stories.

entries.title: The Wire
entries.subtitle: A Baltimore investigation reveals the institutions surrounding it
entries.summary: The Wire begins with a Baltimore police investigation and gradually takes in the institutions that shape the city. David Simon follows the working routines of investigators and those they pursue, then expands the story to docks, politics, schools and journalism.
body: David Simon's The Wire begins with police trying to understand a drug organisation in Baltimore. First broadcast on HBO in the United States on 2 June 2002, it follows investigators and the people they pursue as inhabitants of the same city. The story gradually reaches the docks, local government, schools and a newspaper, showing how the original investigation fits within a wider network of institutions.

Police work often depends on patient observation and learning how people communicate. Building a useful case can take more time than senior officers are prepared to allow, while pressure for quick results alters what counts as success. On the streets, people face comparable pressures within their own hierarchies and routines. These parallels help explain decisions while preserving the differences in their consequences and the responsibility of those who make them.

Across five seasons, characters carry their experience from one institution to another. A reform may solve an immediate problem and reveal a limit elsewhere; personal competence offers no guarantee of lasting influence. Simon's background as a Baltimore reporter informs the precise language of work and place. The continuing story gives minor encounters time to matter. A conversation or administrative decision may reveal its full significance only when its effects have spread to other parts of the city.
story_headings: Police and suspects within the same city
When immediate results shape the work
Consequences that travel across five seasons

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
entries.subtitle: A hidden chamber makes Hogwarts a place of suspicion
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets turns the familiar school into the setting for a series of unexplained attacks. Harry searches for their source as suspicion falls on him, and accounts of the past offer competing explanations.
body: Harry returns to Hogwarts despite attempts by the house-elf Dobby to keep him away. Students are soon found petrified, raising fears that a hidden chamber has been opened. Chris Columbus again directs Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint and Emma Watson, with Kenneth Branagh joining as the boastful Gilderoy Lockhart and Jason Isaacs as Lucius Malfoy. Released in Britain and the United States on 15 November 2002, the second film follows Harry's investigation of the attacks while suspicion increasingly settles on him.

Familiar classrooms and corridors become places to look for clues. A diary draws Harry into another person's account of the past, while the Forbidden Forest brings him to a much larger creature and another version of events. The forest, assembled from location and studio filming in the first film, was recreated entirely in the studio for this one to accommodate Aragog's lair. John Williams's score adds new musical identities, including Fawkes the Phoenix, alongside the themes that already connect the audience to Hogwarts.
story_headings: Dobby's warning and the attacks at school
A diary, a forest and conflicting accounts

entries.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
entries.subtitle: The divided Fellowship follows several paths through Middle-earth
entries.summary: The Two Towers continues Peter Jackson's Tolkien trilogy with the Fellowship divided. Its interwoven journeys bring the war in Rohan alongside Frodo and Sam's increasingly difficult route towards Mordor, where they must depend on Gollum as their guide.
body: The Two Towers opened in American cinemas on 18 December 2002, continuing Peter Jackson's adaptation of J. R. R. Tolkien. Frodo and Sam accept Gollum as a guide towards Mordor; Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli become involved in Rohan's defence; Merry and Pippin meet Treebeard and the Ents. With the Fellowship divided, the film moves between their journeys. The growing war unfolds alongside the smaller and increasingly difficult task of carrying the Ring.

Gollum brings an unstable presence to Frodo and Sam's journey. Andy Serkis supplied the performance that formed the basis of the digital character, while Weta Digital developed animation and rendering techniques to convey his movements and expressions. Gollum's arguments with himself bring the struggle over the Ring into one character. Frodo recognises someone damaged by a burden he now shares. Sam distrusts the guide on whom their route increasingly depends.

The defence of Rohan culminates in a prolonged night battle at Helm's Deep. Rain, ladders, walls and a breached gate give the siege a clear physical geography as the armies grow. Weta's work combined the large battle with digital characters across hundreds of effects shots, earning the Academy Award for Visual Effects. Howard Shore's score gives Rohan a musical identity of its own, including the fiddle in The Riders of Rohan, alongside themes carried over from the first film.
story_headings: Three journeys after the Fellowship breaks
Gollum's performance and divided loyalties

entries.title: Human Genome Project
entries.summary: The Human Genome Project was an international effort to identify, map and sequence human DNA. Its completion in 2003 covered about 92% of the genome; later work addressed the difficult remaining regions, including the highly repetitive Y chromosome.
body:
The Human Genome Project was declared complete on 14 April 2003. Launched in 1990 after early planning discussions began in 1984, the international collaboration set out to identify and map human genes and determine the order of the base pairs that make up human DNA. The sequence produced by the project covered about 92% of the genome.

Sequencing continued after the project's conclusion. Work presented in 2021 helped resolve the remaining regions, leading to the publication in March 2022 of a gapless sequence of the twenty-two autosomes and the X chromosome. Repetitive DNA made the Y chromosome particularly difficult to assemble; its complete sequence was published in August 2023.
story_headings: From the 2003 completion to the remaining gaps

provenance.full_source_extract:
The Human Genome Project (HGP) was an international scientific research project with the goal of determining the base pairs that make up human DNA, and of identifying, mapping and sequencing all of the genes of the human genome from both a physical and a functional standpoint. It started in 1990 and was completed in 2003. It was the world's largest collaborative biological project. Planning for the project began in 1984 by the US government, and it officially launched in 1990. It was declared complete on 14 April 2003, and included about 92% of the genome. Level "complete genome" was achieved in May 2021, with only 0.3% of the bases covered by potential issues. The full gapless sequence containing 22 autosomes and the X chromosome was published in January 2022, making it the first fully sequenced human genome. The full sequence of the Y chromosome was only published in August 2023 due to challenges with sequencing and assembling, caused by its highly repetitive nature.
Funding came from the US government through the National Institutes of Health (NIH) as well as numerous other groups from around the world. A parallel project was conducted outside the government by the Celera Corporation, or Celera Genomics, which was formally launched in 1998. Most of the government-sponsored sequencing was performed in twenty universities and research centres in the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, France, Germany, and China, working in the International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium (IHGSC).
The Human Genome Project originally aimed to map the complete set of nucleotides contained in a human haploid reference genome, of which there are more than three billion. The genome of any given individual is unique; mapping the human genome involved sequencing samples collected from a small number of individuals and then assembling the sequenced fragments to get a complete sequence for each of the 23 human chromosome pairs (22 pairs of autosomes and a pair of sex chromosomes, known as allosomes). Therefore, the finished human genome is a mosaic, not representing any one individual. Much of the project's utility comes from the fact that the vast majority of the human genome is the same in all humans.

entries.title: Iraq War
entries.summary: The Iraq War began with a US-led invasion in 2003 that overthrew Saddam Hussein. Occupation and insurgency prolonged the fighting until the American withdrawal in 2011, with further armed conflict continuing afterwards.
body: The Iraq War began on 20 March 2003, when a United States-led coalition launched air strikes against Iraq. Britain, Australia and Poland joined the operation, which overthrew Saddam Hussein's Ba'athist government. President George W. Bush had obtained congressional authority to use force in October 2002, within his administration's wider war-on-terror policy. The invasion was followed by an occupation in which insurgents fought both coalition troops and the newly established Iraqi government. Fighting continued until American forces withdrew in 2011, and Iraq remained affected by armed conflict after their departure.
story_headings: From the invasion to the American withdrawal

images.title: BAGHDAD, IRAQ (November 2003) - U.S. Army (USA) M1A1 Abrams MBT (Main Battle Tank), and personnel from A Company (CO), Task Force 1st Battalion, 35th Armor Regiment (1-35 Armor), 2nd Brigade Combat Team (BCT), 1st Armored Division (AD), pose for a photo under the " Victory Arch " in Ceremony Square, Baghdad, Iraq during Operation Iraqi Freedom. The Hands of Victory monument built at the end of the Iran-Iraq war marks the entrance to a large parade ground in central Baghdad. The hand and arm are modeled after former dictator Saddam Husseins own and surrounded with thousands of Iranian helmets taken from the battlefield. The swords made from the guns of dead Iraqi soldiers, melted and recast into the 24-ton blades.

provenance.full_source_extract:
The Iraq War (Arabic: حرب العراق, romanized: ḥarb al-ʿirāq), also referred to as the Second Gulf War (Gulf War II), was a protracted armed conflict in Iraq from 2003 to 2011. It began in March 2003 with the invasion by a United States–led coalition, which resulted in the overthrow of the Ba'athist government of Saddam Hussein. During the US occupation of Iraq, the conflict persisted as an insurgency that arose against coalition forces and the newly established Iraqi government. US forces were officially withdrawn in 2011. In 2014, the US became re-engaged in Iraq, leading a new coalition under Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve, as the conflict evolved into the ongoing Islamic State insurgency.
The Iraq invasion was part of the Bush administration's broader war on terror, launched in response to the September 11 attacks. In October 2002, the US Congress passed a bipartisan resolution granting Bush authority to use military force against Iraq. The war began on March 20, 2003, when the US, joined by the UK, Australia, and Poland, initiated a "shock and awe" bombing campaign. Coalition forces launched a ground invasion, defeating Iraqi forces and toppling the Ba'athist regime. Saddam Hussein was captured in 2003 and executed in 2006.
The fall of Saddam's regime created a power vacuum, which, along with the Coalition Provisional Authority's mismanagement, fueled a sectarian civil war between Iraq's Shia majority and Sunni minority, and contributed to a lengthy insurgency. In response, the US deployed an additional 170,000 troops during the 2007 troop surge, which helped stabilize parts of the country. In 2008, Bush agreed to withdraw US combat troops, a process completed in 2011 under President Barack Obama.
Among the international law justifications advanced by the United States for the Iraq War were the inherent right of anticipatory self-defense and prior authorization by the Security Council. The primary rationale for the invasion centered around false claims that Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction (WMDs) and that Saddam Hussein was supporting al-Qaeda. The 9/11 Commission concluded in 2004 that there was no credible evidence linking Saddam to al-Qaeda, and no WMD stockpiles were found in Iraq. These false claims faced widespread criticism, in the US and abroad. Kofi Annan, then secretary-general of the United Nations, declared the invasion illegal under international law, as it violated the UN Charter. The 2016 Chilcot Report, a British inquiry, concluded the war was unnecessary, as peaceful alternatives had not been fully explored. Iraq held multi-party elections in 2005, and Nouri al-Maliki became Prime Minister in 2006, a position he held until 2014. His government's policies alienated Iraq's Sunni minority, exacerbating sectarian tensions.
The war led to an estimated 150,000 to over a million deaths, including over 100,000 civilians, with most occurring during the post-invasion insurgency and civil war. The war had lasting geopolitical effects, including the emergence of the extremist Islamic State, whose rise led to the 2013–2017 War in Iraq. The war damaged American international reputation, and Bush's popularity declined. UK prime minister Tony Blair's support for the war diminished his standing, contributing to his resignation in 2007.

entries.title: Roman Polanski wins his first Oscar
entries.subtitle: The directing award recognises The Pianist
entries.summary: The Pianist brought Roman Polanski his first Oscar for a film centred on a musician's survival in wartime Warsaw. Its attention to shelter, waiting and daily needs carries the story through the city's destruction.
body: Roman Polanski won his first Oscar on 23 March 2003, receiving the directing award for The Pianist. The film follows Władysław Szpilman, a Polish Jewish musician trying to survive the destruction of Warsaw during the Holocaust. Polanski did not attend the ceremony; presenter Harrison Ford accepted the award on his behalf.

Adrien Brody plays Szpilman as his world steadily contracts. His professional life gives way to confinement, separation and hiding among the ruins of Warsaw. Ronald Harwood adapted the pianist's memoir, following a survivor whose safety depends on individual encounters and temporary shelters. Waiting and meeting ordinary needs occupy much of his time. As he moves from one hiding place to another, the city's destruction becomes visible in the spaces where he tries to stay alive.

The Pianist had won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2002. At the 75th Academy Awards, Adrien Brody received the leading actor award and Ronald Harwood won for adapted screenplay, alongside Polanski's directing Oscar. The three honours recognised the performance, writing and direction of the same adaptation. Music runs through Szpilman's identity even when public performance is impossible. His ability to play endures, so his eventual return to a keyboard carries the weight of what he has survived.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
entries.subtitle: Official denial reaches the classrooms of Hogwarts
entries.summary: In Rowling's fifth Harry Potter novel, official denial of Voldemort's return reaches Hogwarts through Dolores Umbridge. Restrictions on teaching lead students to organise their own training, while Harry struggles with anger, isolation and the reliability of his perceptions.
body: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix was published on 21 June 2003, after Bloomsbury and Scholastic jointly announced its release. J. K. Rowling's fifth novel begins with a wizarding government refusing to accept Voldemort's return. Harry's account is challenged, and the Ministry extends its influence into Hogwarts through Dolores Umbridge. Her restrictions affect what pupils can learn and say. Beyond the school, the Order brings together people prepared to oppose Voldemort.

Harry and his friends organise their own practical training when their defence lessons fail to prepare them. Learning together gives classmates a place to practise the skills withheld by official teaching and a reason to trust one another. Harry's anger and isolation make his role in the group difficult, while his connection to Voldemort leaves him uncertain about his own perceptions. Rowling brings the public dispute over events into a teenager's private life: exams, friendships and authority all add to the strain of an increasingly frustrated school year.

entries.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
entries.subtitle: The divided Fellowship reaches the end of its journey
entries.summary: The Return of the King concludes Peter Jackson's Tolkien trilogy by bringing the war against Sauron alongside the final approach to Mount Doom. The scale of the battles shares the screen with exhaustion, loyalty and the difficulty of returning home.
body: The Return of the King opened in American cinemas on 17 December 2003, following its world premiere in Wellington on 1 December. Peter Jackson's third Tolkien film brings the divided Fellowship's journeys towards their conclusion. Frodo and Sam approach Mount Doom with Gollum as their guide, while Gandalf helps defend Minas Tirith and Aragorn takes his place among the leaders opposing Sauron. The film moves between armies gathering for battle and two exhausted travellers whose task still requires them to reach the mountain.

Minas Tirith extends the scale of siege warfare seen at Helm's Deep. A city rising in tiers faces siege engines, flying creatures and armies on the Pelennor Fields. Meanwhile, Frodo's strength and judgement continue to falter. Sam's persistence keeps them moving towards Mount Doom, giving their journey a personal urgency within the wider war. At the Black Gate, the military campaign becomes a diversion designed to give the two travellers a chance to complete their task.

After the fighting, the film gives time to the return home and the departures that follow. The hobbits reach the Shire carrying experiences their neighbours have barely noticed, while Frodo's wounds remain part of the ending. Howard Shore's music connects these farewells with themes developed across the trilogy. The three films had appeared in consecutive years, and the final instalment won eleven Oscars in 2004, including Best Picture, Directing, Original Score and Original Song.

entries.title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
entries.summary: The Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004 followed an undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra. Coastal communities across fourteen countries suffered destruction, leaving survivors to rebuild homes, services and livelihoods after the deadliest tsunami in recorded history.
body: An undersea earthquake struck off Aceh in northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. A rupture at a boundary between tectonic plates caused the earthquake, which the US Geological Survey measures at magnitude 9.1. It generated a tsunami that crossed the Indian Ocean. Waves of around thirty metres were reported in parts of Sumatra. Coastal communities suffered destruction across fourteen countries, with Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand among the worst affected. NOAA records an estimated 227,898 people dead or missing, making it the deadliest recorded tsunami. Across the devastated coastal areas, survivors faced the loss of homes, basic services and livelihoods.
story_headings: Destruction across fourteen countries

provenance.date_note: The requested work/event and its year correspond to the independently reviewed source passage. Exact day/month should only be added when explicitly documented.
provenance.full_source_extract:
On 26 December 2004, at 07:58:53 local time (UTC+7), a Mw 9.2–9.3 earthquake struck with its epicenter off the west coast of Aceh, in northern Sumatra, Indonesia. The undersea megathrust earthquake, known in the scientific community as the Sumatra–Andaman earthquake, was caused by a rupture along the fault boundary between the Burma plate and the Indian plate, and reached a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX in some areas.
The earthquake caused a massive tsunami with waves up to 30 m (100 ft) high, referred to by British and Commonwealth media as the Boxing Day tsunami, after the Boxing Day holiday, or the Asian tsunami, which devastated communities along the surrounding coasts of the Indian Ocean, killing an estimated 227,898 people in 14 countries, especially in Aceh in Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Tamil Nadu in India, and Khao Lak in Thailand. The direct result was severe disruption to living conditions and commerce in coastal provinces of these and other surrounding countries. It is the deadliest tsunami in history, the deadliest natural disaster of the 21st century, and one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history. It is also the worst natural disaster in the history of Indonesia, the Maldives, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.
The earthquake itself is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded in Asia, the strongest of the 21st century, and the second- or third-most powerful globally since modern seismography began in 1900. It had the longest fault rupture ever observed, between 1,200 to 1,300 kilometres (746 to 808 mi), and had the longest duration of faulting ever observed, lasting at least ten minutes. Its seismic waves caused measurable vibrations throughout the planet, with displacements of up to 10 mm (0.4 in), and also remotely triggered earthquakes as far away as Alaska. Its epicentre was located between Simeulue and mainland Sumatra. The plight of the affected people and countries prompted a worldwide humanitarian response, with donations totaling more than US$14 billion (equivalent to US$24 billion in 2025 currency).

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
entries.subtitle: Alfonso Cuarón brings colder weather and shifting perspectives to Hogwarts
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban brings an escaped prisoner and the Dementors into Harry's third school year. Under Alfonso Cuarón, changing perspectives and repeated moments reshape the mystery, while the landscape and weather make Hogwarts feel more exposed.
body: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban opened in Britain and Ireland on 31 May 2004, followed by the United States on 4 June. Harry learns that the escaped prisoner Sirius Black may be coming for him. Dementors guard Hogwarts, but their presence draws him back towards his parents' deaths. Alfonso Cuarón directs this third film with cinematographer Michael Seresin and screenwriter Steve Kloves. Gary Oldman plays Black, David Thewlis joins as Professor Lupin and Michael Gambon takes over as Dumbledore.

Events first shown without their full context return with new information. Familiar sounds and movements acquire another meaning as Harry and Hermione take an active part in revisiting what the audience has already seen. Time and perspective thus shape the action. Hogwarts also feels more exposed to the weather and surrounding landscape, while Dementors interrupt familiar journeys and games. John Williams's A Window to the Past brings a quieter musical presence to the film, linking Harry's immediate fears to the family history he is trying to understand.

entries.title: Hurricane Katrina
entries.summary: Hurricane Katrina devastated parts of the southeastern United States in August 2005, with especially severe damage around New Orleans. Its path through Florida and the Gulf of Mexico ended in one of the country's costliest disasters.
body: Katrina formed as a tropical depression near the Bahamas on 23 August 2005, crossed southeastern Florida and rapidly intensified over the Gulf of Mexico. It reached Louisiana and Mississippi on 29 August, bringing particularly severe destruction to New Orleans and the surrounding region. The storm caused 1,392 deaths and an estimated 125 billion US dollars in damage, measured in 2005 prices. At the time, it was the deadliest hurricane to strike the United States since 1928. Its financial losses also placed it among the country's costliest disasters, and the name Katrina became closely associated with the devastation around New Orleans.
story_headings: Katrina reaches Louisiana and Mississippi

images.title: Hurricane Katrina on August 28, 2005
images.creator: NASA

sources.title: Hurricane Katrina — English Wikipedia, revision 1381172866
sources.attribution: Text excerpt from English Wikipedia; CC BY-SA 4.0. Revision and contributor history retained.

provenance.date_note: The requested work/event and its year correspond to the independently reviewed source passage. Exact day/month should only be added when explicitly documented.
provenance.full_source_extract:
Hurricane Katrina was an extremely powerful and catastrophic tropical cyclone that affected the Southeastern United States in late August 2005, particularly in and around the city of New Orleans. Katrina became the United States' costliest tropical cyclone, with an estimated $125 billion ($206 billion when adjusted for inflation) in damages. The hurricane killed 1,392 people, making it the deadliest American hurricane since the 1928 Okeechobee hurricane and is the only mainland U.S. hurricane to have killed over a thousand people since then. Katrina was the twelfth tropical cyclone, the fifth hurricane, the third major hurricane, and the second Category 5 hurricane of the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season. It was also the fourth-most intense Atlantic hurricane to make landfall in the contiguous United States, as measured by barometric pressure.
The hurricane originated on August 23 near the Bahamas, from the merger of a tropical wave and the remnants of a tropical depression. Katrina strengthened into a hurricane before making its first landfall in southeast Florida on August 25. Crossing the state, the hurricane entered the Gulf of Mexico on August 26 and rapidly intensified. Early on August 28, Katrina peaked as a Category 5 hurricane, with winds of 175 mph (280 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 902 mbar (26.64 inHg). Turning to the north, the hurricane weakened to a Category 3 hurricane before making landfall on August 29 near Buras-Triumph, Louisiana, with a subsequent final landfall near the Louisiana–Mississippi border. Katrina also produced a widespread tornado outbreak while moving inland and weakening. On August 31, a cold front over Ohio absorbed the circulation of the former hurricane. The remnants of Katrina continued to the northeast, later moving through Canada before losing their identity on September 7 over the eastern Great Lakes.
Eighty percent of New Orleans, as well as large areas in neighboring parishes, were flooded. It is estimated that about 97,000 people remained in the City of New Orleans, despite mandatory evacuation orders. The flooding prompted a massive national and international response effort, including federal, local, and private rescue operations. The largest loss of life was due to flooding caused by engineering flaws in the federally built hurricane protection system, particularly the levees around New Orleans. Investigators concluded that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, tasked by Congress in the Flood Control Act of 1965 to design and build the region's hurricane protection, was responsible for the breached floodwalls. Later, a federal appeals court ruled that the Army Corps, despite being responsible, could not be held financially liable due to the Flood Control Act of 1928.
The preparation and emergency response from federal, state, and local governments was widely criticized, leading to the resignation of Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) director Michael D. Brown. President George W. Bush also faced criticism. However, several agencies, such as the United States Coast Guard (USCG), National Hurricane Center (NHC), and National Weather Service (NWS), were commended for their actions. The destruction and loss of life caused by the storm prompted the name Katrina to be retired by the World Meteorological Organization in April 2006.

Katrina was the twelfth tropical cyclone, the fifth hurricane, the third major hurricane, and the second Category 5 hurricane of the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season. It was also the fourth-most intense Atlantic hurricane to make landfall in the contiguous United States, as measured by barometric pressure.

entries.title: YouTube
entries.summary: YouTube brought video uploads and viewing together on one online platform. As its audience grew, individuals and organisations gained a widely used route for publishing music, entertainment and other recorded material, supported by advertising, revenue sharing and subscriptions.
body: Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim and Steve Chen founded YouTube in February 2005. The video-sharing service opened to the public in beta that May, giving users a place both to upload material and to watch videos. Google completed its acquisition in November 2006 in a deal valued at 1.65 billion US dollars. Advertising, revenue sharing with creators and later paid subscriptions supported the platform's expansion. As audiences and uploads grew, video publishing became an everyday activity for individuals and organisations, and YouTube developed into a major channel for music, entertainment and other recorded material.

provenance.full_source_extract:
YouTube  is an American online video-sharing platform owned by Google. YouTube was founded on February 14, 2005, by Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim, and Steve Chen, all of whom were former employees at PayPal. Headquartered in San Bruno, California, it is the second-most-visited website in the world, after Google itself. In January 2024, YouTube had reached more than 2.7 billion monthly active users, who collectively watched more than one billion hours of video every day. As of May 2019, videos were being uploaded to the platform at a rate of more than 500 hours of video per minute, and as of mid-2024, there were approximately 14.8 billion videos in total.
On November 13, 2006, YouTube was purchased by Google for 1.65 billion USD (equivalent to $2.44 billion in 2025). Google expanded YouTube's business model from generating revenue through advertisements alone to paid offerings such as movies and exclusive programming explicitly produced for YouTube. It also offers YouTube Premium, a paid subscription option for watching videos without ads. YouTube incorporated the Google AdSense program, generating more revenue for both YouTube and approved users. In 2025, YouTube's advertising revenue was $40.4 billion.
Since its purchase by Google, YouTube has expanded beyond the core website, creating mobile apps, network television, games, and the ability to link with other platforms. Video categories on YouTube include music videos, video clips, news, short and feature films, songs, documentaries, movie trailers, teasers, TV spots, live streams, vlogs, and more. Most submissions are generated by individuals, including collaborations between YouTubers and corporate sponsors. Established media, news, and entertainment corporations have also created and expanded their visibility on YouTube channels to reach bigger audiences.
YouTube has had unprecedented social impact, influencing popular culture, internet trends, and creating multimillionaire celebrities. Despite its growth and success, the platform has been criticized for its facilitation of the spread of misinformation and copyrighted material, routinely violating its users' privacy, excessive censorship, endangering the safety of children and their well-being, and for its inconsistent implementation of platform guidelines.

body: Revenge of the Sith finds the Jedi leading clone armies against the Separatists. Anakin Skywalker is caught between his loyalty to the Jedi, his attachment to Padmé and the confidence offered by Chancellor Palpatine. As the war continues, decisions made in those personal relationships become inseparable from the Republic’s political future.

Written and directed by George Lucas, the 2005 film completes the prequel trilogy and connects it to the Imperial galaxy of the original Star Wars. The friendship between Anakin and Obi-Wan gives the wider collapse a personal centre. John Williams’s score, including Battle of the Heroes, accompanies a story in which military victory and private loss develop together.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
entries.subtitle: A borrowed textbook and private lessons in Voldemort's past
entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince follows two kinds of learning in Harry's sixth year. Notes in an old textbook offer immediate help, while Dumbledore's lessons ask him to examine a past whose consequences are still unfolding.
body: J. K. Rowling's sixth Harry Potter novel appeared on 16 July 2005, with a launch at Edinburgh Castle broadcast to audiences around the world. At Hogwarts, a second-hand Potions textbook brings Harry unexpected success. Handwritten improvements help him in class, although he does not know who made them or what their author intended. He also suspects Draco Malfoy of working on something dangerous within the school. These uncertainties run through a sixth year in which friendships and romantic attachments are changing.

Dumbledore's private lessons take Harry into recorded memories of Voldemort's earlier life. Each visit adds to a history whose objects, ambitions and decisions now matter to the coming conflict. Old conversations and apparently minor possessions become part of the investigation. Harry must also judge the authority of his teachers and the appeal of knowledge acquired from someone else. The textbook offers quick answers in class; understanding the past requires patience and judgement. In both cases, he has to consider how well he knows the person guiding him.

entries.summary: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire centres on a school competition that unexpectedly names Harry as an extra champion. Dangerous tasks and the Yule Ball bring public scrutiny into his fourth year, complicating both his friendships and his safety.
body: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire opened in American cinemas on 18 November 2005. Mike Newell directs the fourth film, in which an enchanted cup selects Harry for an international tournament despite his being too young to enter. As an additional champion, he must prepare for a dragon, an underwater search and a maze. Robert Pattinson plays Cedric Diggory, while Brendan Gleeson appears as Alastor Moody, the new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher. Harry's growing public profile brings advantages as well as dangers.

The Yule Ball adds a social demand to the tournament: its champions must dance in front of the other pupils, and finding a partner presents difficulties that magic offers little help with. Movement director Wayne McGregor choreographed the ball and the visiting schools' entrances, giving each group its own physical presence. Patrick Doyle took over from John Williams as composer. His Harry in Winter expands a brief passage heard in the film into a standalone orchestral piece, giving Harry a quieter musical identity amid the tournament's ceremonies and threats.

entries.title: Pluto's reclassification
entries.summary: Pluto became a dwarf planet in 2006 under a new astronomical definition. This icy, rocky body in the Kuiper belt follows a tilted, elongated orbit that can take it closer to the Sun than Neptune.
body:
On 24 August 2006, the International Astronomical Union adopted new criteria for planets and classified Pluto as a dwarf planet. Made mainly of ice and rock, Pluto lies in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune. It has roughly one-sixth of the Moon's mass and one-third of its volume, placing it among the largest known bodies in that region.

Its tilted, elongated orbit carries it between about 30 and 49 astronomical units from the Sun. At its average distance, sunlight takes around five and a half hours to reach it. Pluto sometimes comes closer to the Sun than Neptune does, but a stable resonance between their orbits keeps them from colliding.
story_headings: A dwarf planet on an unusual orbit

provenance.date_note: The requested work/event and its year correspond to the independently reviewed source passage. Exact day/month should only be added when explicitly documented.
provenance.full_source_extract:
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune. It is the ninth-largest and tenth-most-massive known object to directly orbit the Sun. It is the largest known trans-Neptunian object by volume by a small margin, but is less massive than Eris. Like other Kuiper belt objects, Pluto is made primarily of ice and rock and is much smaller than the inner planets. Pluto has roughly one-sixth the mass of the Moon and one-third of its volume. Originally considered a planet, its status was changed when astronomers adopted a new definition of the word with new criteria.
Pluto has a moderately eccentric and inclined orbit, ranging from 30 to 49 astronomical units (4.5 to 7.3 billion kilometres; 2.8 to 4.6 billion miles) from the Sun. Light from the Sun takes 5.5 hours to reach Pluto at its orbital distance of 39.5 AU (5.91 billion km; 3.67 billion mi). Pluto's eccentric orbit periodically brings it closer to the Sun than Neptune, but a stable orbital resonance prevents them from colliding.
Pluto has five known moons: Charon (the largest and the diameter of which is just over half that of Pluto), Styx, Nix, Kerberos, and Hydra. Pluto and Charon are sometimes considered a binary system because the barycenter of their orbits (that is, their center of mass) does not lie within either body, and they are tidally locked. New Horizons was the first spacecraft to visit Pluto and its moons, making a flyby on July 14, 2015, and taking detailed measurements and observations.
Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde W. Tombaugh, making it the first known object in the Kuiper belt. It was immediately hailed as the ninth planet, but its planetary status was questioned when it was found to be much smaller than expected. These doubts increased following the discovery of additional objects in the Kuiper belt starting in the 1990s, particularly the more massive scattered disk object Eris in 2005. In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) formally redefined the term planet to exclude dwarf planets such as Pluto. Many planetary astronomers, however, continue to consider Pluto and other dwarf planets to be planets.
