entries.title: Raspberry Pi
entries.summary: Raspberry Pi put a low-cost computer on a small board, giving schools and hobbyists a tool for learning programming. Its educational beginnings led to uses in robotics, home automation and industry.
body:
Raspberry Pi is a British family of small, single-board computers developed by the Raspberry Pi Foundation with Broadcom. First offered for sale on 29 February 2012, it was created to support computer science teaching in schools. Its size and low cost also made it useful for robotics, home automation, industrial applications and hobby projects. A commercial company, now Raspberry Pi Holdings, was established to meet growing demand.

The wider product range extends from microcontrollers to computers suitable for everyday PC tasks. Connections include HDMI, USB and GPIO pins; wireless networking and memory capacity depend on the model. Many models use microSD cards for storage.

provenance.full_source_extract:
Raspberry Pi ( PY) is a series of small single-board computers (SBCs) originally developed in the United Kingdom by the Raspberry Pi Foundation in collaboration with Broadcom. To commercialize the product and support its growing demand, the Foundation established a commercial entity, now known as Raspberry Pi Holdings.
The Raspberry Pi was originally created to help teach computer science in schools, but gained popularity for many other uses for its low cost, high performance, compact size, and flexibility. It is now used in areas such as industrial automation, robotics, home automation, IoT devices, and hobbyist projects.
The company's products range from simple microcontrollers to computers that the company markets as being powerful enough to be used as a general purpose PC. Computers are built around a custom designed system on a chip and offer features such as HDMI video/audio output, USB ports, wireless networking, GPIO pins, and up to 16 GB of RAM. Storage is typically provided via microSD cards.
In 2015, the Raspberry Pi surpassed the ZX Spectrum as the best-selling British computer of all time. As of March 2026, over 75 million units had been sold.

entries.title: The Avengers
entries.subtitle: Six heroes learn to fight together
entries.summary: The Avengers brings Marvel's separately established heroes into one story. Their conflicting loyalties make cooperation difficult, until the battle for New York gives each character a place in a team whose abilities work together.
body: The Avengers assembles Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow and Hawkeye against Loki. Nick Fury recruits them through S.H.I.E.L.D., bringing together people with different habits and loyalties. Joss Whedon directed the Marvel Studios film, which began its international cinema release on 25 April 2012 and opened in the United States on 4 May.

The earlier films give each hero a recognisable response to the crisis. Tony Stark challenges authority, Steve Rogers acts from a sense of duty, and Thor faces an enemy from his own family. Bruce Banner has to judge how far he can trust his control. Their first exchanges show the difficulties of working together, while those distinct personalities help the audience follow what each brings to the action.

During the New York battle, the heroes turn their differences into a way of fighting together. They cover separate parts of the city, hand threats from one to another and combine abilities established in their individual films. A long moving shot connects several fights in a continuous view of the team. Marvel's shared continuity becomes part of the drama: knowledge of the earlier adventures helps viewers understand this new story about the characters meeting.

entries.title: London 2012 Olympic Games
entries.summary: London hosted the modern Olympic Games for a third time in 2012. A new Olympic Park in Stratford connected the sporting programme with the redevelopment of a former industrial area in the city's east.
body: The London Olympic Games ran from 27 July to 12 August 2012. They brought together 10,568 athletes, with 204 National Olympic Committees represented alongside four independent Olympic athletes. Having hosted in 1908 and 1948, London became the first city to stage the modern Games three times. Preparations turned a former industrial site in Stratford into a 200-hectare Olympic Park, with sustainability central to the redevelopment plans. Existing venues also held competitions, and some events took place elsewhere in Britain. The sporting gathering was thus accompanied by extensive changes to part of East London.
story_headings: A third Olympics and a new Olympic Park

provenance.full_source_extract:
The 2012 Summer Olympics, officially the Games of the XXX Olympiad and also known as London 2012, were an international multi-sport event held from 27 July to 12 August 2012 in London, England. Some events were held at venues elsewhere in the United Kingdom. There were 10,518 athletes from 206 National Olympic Committees (NOCs) who participated in the 2012 Olympics.
Following a bid headed by the former Olympic champion Sebastian Coe and the mayor of London, Ken Livingstone, London was selected as the host city at the 117th IOC Session in Singapore on 6 July 2005, defeating bids from Moscow, New York City, Madrid and Paris. London became the first city to host the modern Olympics three times, having previously hosted the Summer Games in 1908 and 1948. Construction for the Games involved considerable redevelopment, with an emphasis on sustainability. The main focus was a new 200-hectare (490-acre) Olympic Park, constructed on a former industrial site in Stratford, East London. The Games also used venues that already existed before the bid.
The United States topped the medal table, winning the most gold medals (48) and the highest number of medals overall (105). China finished second with a total of 91 medals (38 gold) and Great Britain came third with 65 medals overall (29 gold). Michael Phelps of the United States became the most decorated Olympic athlete of all time, winning his 22nd medal. Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Brunei entered female athletes for the first time, meaning that every currently eligible country has now sent a female competitor to at least one Olympic Games. Women's boxing was included for the first time, and the 2012 Games became the first at which every sport had female competitors.
The Games received considerable praise for their organisation, with the volunteers, the British military and public enthusiasm commended particularly highly. The Games were described as happy and glorious. The opening ceremony, directed by the Academy Award winner Danny Boyle, received widespread acclaim. These were the final Olympic Games under the IOC presidency of Belgian Jacques Rogge, who was succeeded by German Thomas Bach the next year.

entries.title: Oculus Rift launches on Kickstarter
entries.summary: Oculus's 2012 Kickstarter campaign funded an early Rift development kit. The support for Palmer Luckey's virtual-reality headset gave developers and enthusiasts access to hardware on which they could begin exploring VR before the consumer model arrived.
body:
Oculus opened its Rift development-kit campaign on Kickstarter on 1 August 2012. Palmer Luckey's virtual-reality headset project attracted 9,522 backers, raising US$2,437,429 against a US$250,000 goal.

The first kit, DK1, began shipping in March 2013; DK2 followed in 2014. Developers could use these models to create VR software, while enthusiasts could try the technology ahead of the consumer Rift CV1. The line continued through Rift S. In April 2021, Facebook confirmed that remaining stocks generally would not be replenished, although some retailers still had units for sale as the headset was being withdrawn.
story_headings: From pledges to the first development kits

provenance.full_source_extract:
Oculus Rift is a discontinued line of virtual reality headsets developed and manufactured by Oculus VR, a virtual reality company founded by Palmer Luckey. It was the first virtual reality headset to provide a realistic experience at an accessible price, utilizing novel technology to increase quality and reduce cost by orders of magnitude compared to earlier systems. The first headset in the line was the Oculus Rift Development Kit 1 (DK1), released on March 28, 2013. The last was the Oculus Rift S, discontinued in April 2021.
The Rift went through various pre-production models prior to the release of the Oculus Rift CV1, the first Oculus Rift intended for use by the general public. Two of these, the DK1 in early-2013 and DK2 in mid-2014, were intended to provide content developers with a development kit platform to create content for the Rift's eventual consumer release. However, both development kits were purchased by many gaming enthusiasts who wished to get an early preview of the technology. The Rift saw its official consumer release in March 2016 with the Oculus Rift CV1, and was eventually replaced in March 2019 by the Oculus Rift S. The Oculus Rift software library is still compatible with its successor, the Oculus Go and the Oculus Quest.

entries.title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
entries.subtitle: Bilbo joins thirteen dwarves on the road to Erebor
entries.summary: Peter Jackson's The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey follows Bilbo Baggins from his comfortable home into an expedition to recover a lost kingdom. His encounter with Gollum connects this smaller traveller's adventure to The Lord of the Rings.
body: In The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey, the arrival of Gandalf and thirteen dwarves draws Bilbo Baggins away from his comfortable home at Bag End in the Shire to join an expedition as its burglar. Their leader, Thorin Oakenshield, intends to recover Erebor from the dragon Smaug. Peter Jackson cast Martin Freeman as Bilbo, whose reluctance, small stature and inexperience make him an unlikely recruit. The expedition brings him into contact with trolls, goblins and Gollum. Beneath the mountains, the encounter involving Gollum's riddles and the discovery of the ring links Bilbo's journey to The Lord of the Rings.

The film premiered in Wellington on 28 November 2012 and reached French cinemas on 12 December. Jackson's team returned to the New Zealand landscapes and workshops used to create Middle-earth. Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Jackson and Guillermo del Toro received screenplay credits.

Shot in stereoscopic 3D at 48 frames per second, the film was screened in several formats, including high frame rate presentations. Weta Digital used improved facial capture for Gollum. In his exchange with Bilbo, those technical changes serve the scene's tension, letting suspicion, calculation and fear register on the characters' faces.

entries.title: House of Cards
entries.subtitle: Frank and Claire Underwood pursue power in Washington
entries.summary: House of Cards moved a British political drama to Washington, where Frank and Claire Underwood turn marriage into a partnership of ambition. Netflix released its entire first season together, giving viewers immediate access to the unfolding schemes.
body: The American House of Cards adapts an earlier British political drama to Washington. Kevin Spacey and Robin Wright play Frank and Claire Underwood, a married couple whose ambitions also bind them as political partners. Beau Willimon developed the series, and David Fincher directed the opening episodes. All thirteen episodes of the first season became available on Netflix on 1 February 2013 in the territories then served by the platform, including the United States.

Frank's position in Congress gives him influence over decisions largely hidden from public view. A broken promise sets him on a campaign of manipulation involving colleagues, journalists and staff. Speaking directly to the camera, he shares his calculations with viewers while other characters see only what he chooses to reveal. Claire's organisation and ambitions give their partnership another source of power. Cooperation and rivalry repeatedly shape their life together.

With the full season available on release, viewers could move straight from one episode to the next. Netflix's launch announcement presented it as a continuous narrative, a way of watching supported by the production's carefully controlled settings and steadily accumulating schemes. House of Cards became a prominent early example of a streaming service releasing an expensive original drama a whole season at a time.

entries.title: Random Access Memories
entries.summary: Daft Punk's fourth and final studio album revisits American music of the late 1970s and early 1980s. Live instrumental performances and a wide circle of collaborators shape its combination of disco, progressive rock and pop.
body:
Random Access Memories, the fourth and final studio album by French electronic duo Daft Punk, was released by Columbia Records on 17 May 2013. Its tribute to American music of the late 1970s and early 1980s, especially the music of Los Angeles, also informed the packaging and promotion. Billboards, television advertisements and a web series accompanied the release. Recording took place between 2008 and 2012 at Henson, Conway and Capitol Studios in California, Electric Lady Studios in New York, and Gang Recording Studio in Paris.

After the minimal production of Human After All (2005), the duo worked with Chris Caswell to recruit session musicians for live instrumental performances. Electronic instruments were limited to drum machines, a custom-built modular synthesizer and vintage vocoders. The album combines disco, progressive rock and pop, with contributions from Paul Jackson Jr., Giorgio Moroder, Chilly Gonzales, Julian Casablancas, Paul Williams, Caswell, Pharrell Williams, Nile Rodgers, Todd Edwards, Panda Bear and DJ Falcon.
story_headings: Recording an album around live performances

provenance.full_source_extract:
Random Access Memories is the fourth and final studio album by the French electronic music duo Daft Punk. It was released on 17 May 2013 through Columbia Records. The album pays tribute to late 1970s and early 1980s American music, particularly from Los Angeles. This theme is reflected in the packaging and promotional campaign, which included billboards, television advertisements and a web series. Recording sessions took place from 2008 to 2012 at Henson, Conway and Capitol Studios in California, Electric Lady Studios in New York City, and Gang Recording Studio in Paris, France.
Following the minimal production of their previous album, Human After All (2005), Daft Punk recruited session musicians with the help of Chris Caswell to perform live instrumentation and limited the use of electronic instruments to drum machines, a custom-built modular synthesizer and vintage vocoders. It combines disco, progressive rock and pop, with contributions by Paul Jackson Jr., Giorgio Moroder, Chilly Gonzales, Julian Casablancas, Paul Williams, Caswell, Pharrell Williams, Nile Rodgers, Todd Edwards, Panda Bear and DJ Falcon.
Random Access Memories is the only Daft Punk album to top the US Billboard 200, and was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. It also topped the charts in twenty other countries. Its lead single, "Get Lucky", topped the charts in more than 30 countries and became one of the best-selling digital singles of all time. The album appeared on several year-end lists, and won in several categories at the 2014 Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year, Best Dance/Electronica Album, and Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical. "Get Lucky" also won the awards for Record of the Year and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance. In 2020, Rolling Stone ranked Random Access Memories  number 295 on their list of the "500 Greatest Albums of All Time".

entries.title: Edward Snowden: the surveillance disclosures
entries.summary: In June 2013, documents supplied by Edward Snowden exposed the reach of government surveillance programmes. Reporting on the material brought previously hidden methods of collecting communications into an international debate about security and privacy.
body: Edward Snowden's disclosures in June 2013 revealed the extent of global government surveillance programmes. The former intelligence contractor travelled to Hong Kong and supplied classified documents to journalists. They described programmes run by the NSA and the Five Eyes alliance, with cooperation from telecommunications companies and European governments. Reporting by journalists including Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras brought the material before a wide audience. Systems for collecting communications that had operated out of public view became the subject of international scrutiny and debate over national security and individual privacy.

provenance.full_source_extract:
Edward Joseph Snowden (born June 21, 1983) is a former National Security Agency (NSA) intelligence contractor who leaked classified documents revealing the existence of global surveillance programs.
Born in 1983 in Elizabeth City, North Carolina, he attended a community college and later enrolled in a master's programme at the University of Liverpool without finishing it. In 2006, he started working for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and then moved to Dell in 2009, where he managed computer systems for the NSA. In 2013, he worked for two months at Booz Allen Hamilton, with the purpose of gathering more NSA documents.
In May 2013, Snowden flew to Hong Kong, and in early June he revealed thousands of classified NSA documents to journalists Glenn Greenwald, Laura Poitras, Barton Gellman, and Ewen MacAskill. His disclosures revealed numerous global surveillance programs, many run by the NSA and the Five Eyes intelligence alliance with the cooperation of telecommunications companies and European governments, and prompted a cultural discussion about national security and individual privacy.
On June 21, 2013, the United States Department of Justice unsealed charges against Snowden on two counts of violating the Espionage Act of 1917 and theft of government property, following which the Department of State revoked his passport. He stayed in Sheremetyevo International Airport in Moscow for a month before being granted asylum. He became a naturalized Russian citizen in 2022.
In early 2016, Snowden became the president of the Freedom of the Press Foundation, a San Francisco–based nonprofit organization that aims to protect journalists from hacking and government surveillance. He also has a job at an unnamed Russian IT company. In 2017, he married Lindsay Mills. On September 17, 2019, his memoir Permanent Record was published. On September 2, 2020, the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit ruled in United States v. Moalin that one of the U.S. intelligence's mass surveillance programs exposed by Snowden was illegal and possibly unconstitutional.

entries.subtitle: The expedition reaches Erebor and its dragon
entries.summary: The second Hobbit film takes Bilbo and the dwarves through Mirkwood to the kingdom they hope to reclaim. Inside Erebor, their arrival turns a journey towards treasure into a confrontation with the dragon guarding it.
body: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug follows Bilbo and the dwarves through Mirkwood towards the Lonely Mountain. Encounters with spiders, captivity in the elves' kingdom and escape in barrels leave the company increasingly exposed to danger. In Lake-town they meet people living below the lost kingdom, including Bard, played by Luke Evans. Erebor is the expedition's destination, but reclaiming its treasure means waking Smaug. The second film opened in France on 11 December 2013 and in the United States on 13 December.

Benedict Cumberbatch provided Smaug's voice and performance capture, making the dragon watchful and mocking as Bilbo moves through the treasure. Weta Digital created the creature and extensive digital settings for Erebor and Lake-town. The gold surrounds the confrontation and gives Smaug something to move through and disturb as he searches for the intruder. Jackson keeps the danger close to Bilbo's attempts to hide and talk his way out. The encounter's consequences then reach beyond the mountain to the people living below it.

entries.summary: The 2014 Nobel Peace Prize recognised Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi's work for children. Their campaigns in Pakistan and India linked access to education with protection from exploitation, across national and religious boundaries.
body: On 10 October 2014, the Norwegian Nobel Committee named Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi joint Peace Prize laureates. They had confronted different barriers facing children: Malala defended girls' access to education in Pakistan, while Satyarthi worked against child exploitation in India. Having survived a Taliban attack in 2012, Malala continued to speak publicly for education. At seventeen, she became the youngest Nobel laureate. The shared award brought these campaigns together across national and religious boundaries, giving children's rights a central place in its message.

entries.title: Interstellar
entries.summary: Christopher Nolan's Interstellar sends astronauts in search of a habitable world as Earth's crops fail. Scientific advice, large-format photography and physical models help give tangible form to a journey into unfamiliar environments.
body: Interstellar, Christopher Nolan's 2014 film, follows astronauts seeking a new home as crop failures and famine threaten Earth. Matthew McConaughey and Anne Hathaway lead the spacefaring cast. The project began with a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and physicist Kip Thorne, who later became its scientific consultant. Christopher and Jonathan Nolan co-wrote the screenplay. Filming in Canada, Iceland and Los Angeles combined large-format photography, practical models and visual effects. Physical locations and objects gave the cast a setting for a story reaching far beyond Earth.
story_headings: Imagining the journey with a physicist

provenance.full_source_extract:
Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity.
The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg. Thorne served as an executive producer and scientific consultant on the film, and wrote the tie-in book The Science of Interstellar. It was Obst's final film as producer before her death. Cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema shot it on 35 mm film in the Panavision anamorphic format and IMAX 70 mm. It was filmed, beginning in late 2013, in Alberta (Canada), Kirkjubæjarklaustur (a village in Iceland), and Los Angeles. Interstellar uses extensive practical and miniature effects, and the company DNEG created additional visual effects.
Interstellar premiered at the TCL Chinese Theatre, Los Angeles, on October 26, 2014, and was released in theaters in the United States on November 5, and in the United Kingdom on November 7, with Paramount Pictures distributing in the United States and Warner Bros. Pictures distributing in international markets. In the United States, it was first released on film stock, expanding to venues using digital projectors. It was a commercial success, grossing $681 million worldwide during its initial theatrical run, and $782.9 million worldwide with subsequent releases, making it the 10th-highest-grossing film of 2014. The film received generally positive reviews from critics. Among its various accolades, Interstellar was nominated for five awards at the 87th Academy Awards, winning for Best Visual Effects.

entries.title: The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies
entries.subtitle: Erebor's treasure divides those who reclaim it
entries.summary: Peter Jackson's final Hobbit film begins with the consequences of reaching Erebor. While survivors of Smaug's attack need help, Thorin clings to the recovered treasure, and Bilbo tries to prevent the dispute from becoming a war.
body: The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies opens with Smaug attacking Lake-town. Survivors need shelter and supplies, while Thorin holds Erebor and becomes increasingly possessive of its treasure. Bilbo seeks a way through the dispute, but armies gather and the reclaimed kingdom becomes a battlefield. Peter Jackson's final Hobbit film opened in France on 10 December 2014 and North America on 17 December. The expedition has reached its lost home; its central problem is now what that recovery means for the people around it.

Weta Digital created the burning town, water effects, massed armies and digital landscapes around Erebor. Its Army Manager system helped organise the crowds, while the Manuka renderer handled detailed lighting in complex scenes. Within these large encounters, the film follows individual confrontations and the changing relationship between Thorin and Bilbo. Their farewell gives weight to Bilbo's return. He reaches Bag End with an adventure his neighbours scarcely understand, and the ending links the trilogy back to the opening of The Fellowship of the Ring.

entries.title: First observation of gravitational waves
entries.summary: LIGO's two observatories recorded gravitational waves directly for the first time in September 2015. The signal matched a pair of black holes spiralling together and merging, providing a new way to observe such events.
body:
Both LIGO observatories detected the first directly observed gravitational-wave signal on 14 September 2015. The LIGO and Virgo collaborations announced the discovery on 11 February 2016. Earlier evidence had been indirect, drawn from the effects of gravitational waves on the timing of pulsars in binary star systems.

The signal matched general relativity's predictions for two black holes spiralling together, merging and settling into a single remnant. Their estimated masses were about 36 and 29 times the Sun's mass; the resulting black hole had about 62 solar masses. The name GW150914 combines gravitational wave with the observation date, 2015-09-14. It was also the first observation of a binary black hole merger, demonstrating that pairs of stellar-mass black holes exist and can merge within the present age of the universe.
story_headings: GW150914 records a merger and its aftermath

provenance.full_source_extract:
The first direct observation of gravitational waves was made on 14 September 2015 and was announced by the LIGO and Virgo collaborations on 11 February 2016. Previously, gravitational waves had been inferred only indirectly, via their effect on the timing of pulsars in binary star systems. The waveform, detected by both LIGO observatories, matched the predictions of general relativity for a gravitational wave emanating from the inward spiral and merger of two black holes (of 36 M☉ and 29 M☉) and the subsequent ringdown of a single, 62 M☉ black hole remnant. The signal was named GW150914 (from gravitational wave and the date of observation 2015-09-14). It was also the first observation of a binary black hole merger, demonstrating both the existence of binary stellar-mass black hole systems and the fact that such mergers could occur within the current age of the universe.
This first direct observation was reported around the world as a remarkable accomplishment for many reasons. Efforts to directly prove the existence of such waves had been ongoing for over fifty years, and the waves are so minuscule that Albert Einstein himself doubted that they could ever be detected. The waves given off by the cataclysmic merger of GW150914 reached Earth as a ripple in spacetime that changed the length of a 1,120 km LIGO effective span by a thousandth of the width of a proton, proportionally equivalent to changing the distance to the nearest star outside the Solar System by one hair's width. The energy released by the binary as it spiralled together and merged was immense, with the energy of 3.0+0.5−0.5 c2 M☉ (5.3+0.9−0.8×1047 joules or 5300+900−800 foes) in total radiated as gravitational waves, reaching a peak emission rate in its final few milliseconds of about 3.6+0.5−0.4×1049 watts – a level greater than the combined power of all light radiated by all the stars in the observable universe.
The observation confirmed the last remaining directly undetected prediction of general relativity and corroborated its predictions of space-time distortion in the context of large scale cosmic events (known as strong field tests). It was heralded as inaugurating a new era of gravitational-wave astronomy, which enables observations of violent astrophysical events that were not previously accessible and allows for the direct observation of the earliest history of the universe. On 15 June 2016, two more detections of gravitational waves, made in late 2015, were announced. Eight more observations were made in 2017, including GW170817, the first observed merger of binary neutron stars, which was also observed in electromagnetic radiation.

entries.title: Paris Agreement
entries.summary: The Paris Agreement established common climate goals through negotiations involving 196 parties in 2015. It links efforts to limit warming with adaptation and finance, while participation has changed through ratifications and withdrawals.
body:
The Paris Agreement emerged from negotiations among 196 parties at the 2015 UN climate conference near Paris. Adopted on 12 December 2015 and opened for signature in 2016, it addresses climate-change mitigation, adaptation and finance. Its goals are to keep warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. These are long-term temperature goals; the IPCC's 2023 assessment measures warming levels using twenty-year averages.

By 27 January 2026, the agreement had 194 parties. The United States withdrew in 2020, rejoined in 2021 and withdrew again on that date in 2026. Iran, a major emitter among members of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, had still not ratified the agreement.
story_headings: Temperature goals and changing participation

provenance.full_source_extract:
The Paris Agreement (also called the Paris Accords or Paris Climate Accords) is an international treaty on climate change that was signed in 2016. The treaty covers climate change mitigation, adaptation, and finance. The Paris Agreement was negotiated by 196 parties at the 2015 United Nations Climate Change Conference near Paris, France. As of January 2026, 194 members of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) are parties to the agreement. Of the three UNFCCC member states which have not ratified the agreement, the only major emitter is Iran. The United States, the second largest emitter, withdrew from the agreement in 2020, rejoined in 2021, and withdrew again in 2026.
The Paris Agreement has a long-term temperature goal which is to keep the rise in global surface temperature to well below 2 °C (3.6 °F) above pre-industrial levels. The treaty also states that preferably the limit of the increase should only be 1.5 °C (2.7 °F). These limits are defined as averages of the global temperature measured over twenty years. 
The lower the temperature increase, the smaller the effects of climate change can be expected. To achieve this temperature goal, greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced as soon as, and by as much as, possible. They should even reach net zero by the middle of the 21st century. To stay below 1.5 °C of global warming, emissions need to be cut by roughly 50% by 2030. This figure takes into account each country's documented pledges.  After the Paris Agreement was signed, global emissions continued to rise rather than fall. 2024 was the hottest year on record, with a rise of more than 1.5 °C in global average temperature. 
The treaty aims to help countries adapt to climate change effects, and mobilize enough finance. Under the agreement, each country must determine, plan, and regularly report on its contributions. No mechanism forces a country to set specific emissions targets, but each target should go beyond previous targets. In contrast to the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, the distinction between developed and developing countries is blurred, so that the latter also have to submit plans for emission reductions.
The Paris Agreement was opened for signature on 22 April 2016 (Earth Day) at a ceremony inside the UN headquarters in New York City. After the European Union ratified the agreement, sufficient countries had ratified the agreement responsible for enough of the world's greenhouse gases for the agreement to enter into force on 4 November 2016.
World leaders have lauded the agreement. However, there is debate about its effectiveness, with some environmentalists and analysts criticizing it for not being strict enough. While pledges under the Paris Agreement are insufficient for reaching the set temperature goals, there is a mechanism of increased ambition. The Paris Agreement has been successfully used in climate litigation in the late 2010s, forcing countries and oil companies to strengthen climate action.

entries.title: Star Wars: Episode VII – The Force Awakens
entries.summary: A scavenger, a former stormtrooper and a droid carrying information about Luke Skywalker become involved in the Resistance’s struggle against the First Order.
story_headings: Rey and Finn enter a new conflict
A new generation meets the original heroes
body: The Force Awakens takes place thirty years after the second Death Star’s destruction. Rey, a scavenger on Jakku, and Finn, a stormtrooper who has fled the First Order, become involved in returning the droid BB-8 to the Resistance. The droid carries information about Luke Skywalker, whose disappearance connects their journey to Leia’s fight against a new enemy.

J.J. Abrams directs the 2015 opening of the sequel trilogy. Han Solo and Chewbacca join the new protagonists, linking an unfamiliar generation to people shaped by the earlier war. John Williams returns to the score and introduces Rey’s Theme, giving the new heroine a musical identity within a series already associated with recurring orchestral themes.

entries.title: Ennio Morricone: the Oscar for The Hateful Eight
entries.summary: Ennio Morricone's score for The Hateful Eight won him a competitive Oscar in 2016, following his honorary award in 2007. The recognition added another chapter to a career spanning hundreds of film and television scores.
body: Ennio Morricone won the Academy Award for Original Score for The Hateful Eight on 28 February 2016. The competitive prize followed his honorary Oscar of 2007. Alongside classical compositions, he had written more than four hundred scores for cinema and television. His partnerships included Sergio Leone's films from A Fistful of Dollars onwards and Giuseppe Tornatore's from Cinema Paradiso. The award recognised a new score from a composer whose music was already associated with several generations of cinema.

provenance.full_source_extract:
Ennio Morricone (10 November 1928 – 6 July 2020) was an Italian composer, orchestrator, conductor, trumpeter, and pianist who wrote music in a wide range of styles. With more than 400 scores for cinema and television, as well as more than 100 classical works, Morricone is widely considered one of the most prolific and greatest film composers of all time. He received numerous accolades throughout his career, including two Academy Awards, three Grammy Awards, three Golden Globes, six BAFTAs, ten David di Donatello, eleven Nastro d'Argento, two European Film Awards, the Golden Lion Honorary Award, and the Polar Music Prize.
His filmography includes more than 70 award-winning films, all of Sergio Leone's films from A Fistful of Dollars on, all of Giuseppe Tornatore's films since Cinema Paradiso, Dario Argento's Animal Trilogy, as well as The Battle of Algiers (1966), 1900 (1976), La Cage aux Folles (1978), Le Professionnel (1981), The Thing (1982), The Key (1983) by Tinto Brass and Tie Me Up! Tie Me Down! (1989). He received the Academy Award for Best Original Score nominations for Days of Heaven (1978), The Mission (1986), The Untouchables (1987), Bugsy (1991), Malèna (2000) and The Hateful Eight (2015), winning for the last. He won the Academy Honorary Award in 2007. His score to The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966) is regarded as one of the most influential soundtracks in history. It was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2008.
After playing the trumpet in jazz bands in the 1940s, Morricone became a studio arranger for RCA Victor and in 1955 started ghost writing for film and theatre. Throughout his career, he composed music for artists such as Paul Anka, Mina, Milva, Zucchero, and Andrea Bocelli. From 1960 to 1975, he gained international fame for composing music for Westerns and—with an estimated 10 million copies sold—Once Upon a Time in the West is one of the best-selling scores worldwide. From 1966 to 1980, he was a main member of Il Gruppo, one of the first experimental composers collectives. In 1969, he co-founded Forum Music Village, a prestigious recording studio. He continued to compose music for European productions, such as Marco Polo, La piovra, Nostromo, Fateless, Karol, and En mai, fais ce qu'il te plait.
Morricone composed for Hollywood directors such as Don Siegel, Mike Nichols, Brian De Palma, Barry Levinson, William Friedkin, Oliver Stone, Warren Beatty, John Carpenter, and Quentin Tarantino. He has also worked with directors such as Bernardo Bertolucci, Mauro Bolognini, Tinto Brass, Giuliano Montaldo, Roland Joffé, Wolfgang Petersen, Roman Polanski, Henri Verneuil, Mario Bava, Lucio Fulci, Umberto Lenzi, Gillo Pontecorvo, and Pier Paolo Pasolini. His best-known compositions include "The Ecstasy of Gold", "Se telefonando", "Man with a Harmonica", "Here's to You", "Chi mai", "Gabriel's Oboe", and "E più ti penso". He has influenced many artists including Hans Zimmer, Danger Mouse, Dire Straits, Muse, Metallica, Fields of the Nephilim, and Radiohead.
On May 10, 2016, Mondadori Libri published his official autobiography, Ennio Morricone. Inseguendo quel suono. La mia musica, la mia vita. Written in conversation with Alessandro De Rosa, the book has been reprinted several times in Italy, translated into the world’s major languages, transcribed and published in English under the title Ennio Morricone: In His Own Words by Oxford University Press in 2019, and described by Morricone himself in the preface as “the best book ever written about me, the most authentic, the most detailed and well curated. The truest.”

entries.title: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
entries.summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Go champion Lee Sedol four games to one in March 2016. The match made artificial intelligence's progress visible through a contest against an expert player, with Lee securing the fourth game.
body: AlphaGo played Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul from 9 to 15 March 2016. DeepMind's program won four of the five games; Lee won the fourth, and every game ended in resignation. The contest became a widely discussed moment in artificial intelligence, inviting comparisons with Deep Blue's 1997 chess match against Garry Kasparov. DeepMind announced that the million-dollar winner's prize would be donated to charities and Go organisations. The Korea Baduk Association recognised AlphaGo's achievement with an honorary ninth-dan rank.
story_headings: A four-to-one result

provenance.full_source_extract:
AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol, also known as the DeepMind Challenge Match, was a five-game Go match between top Go player Lee Sedol and AlphaGo, a computer Go program developed by DeepMind, played in Seoul, South Korea between the 9th and 15th of March 2016. AlphaGo won all but the fourth game; all games were won by resignation. The match has been compared with the historic chess match between Deep Blue and Garry Kasparov in 1997.
The winner of the match was slated to win $1 million. Since AlphaGo won, Google DeepMind stated that the prize would be donated to charities, including UNICEF, and Go organisations. Lee received $170,000 ($150,000 for participating in the five games and an additional $20,000 for winning one game).
After the match, the Korea Baduk Association awarded AlphaGo the highest Go grandmaster rank – an "honorary 9 dan". It was given in recognition of AlphaGo's "sincere efforts" to master Go. This match was chosen by Science as one of the runners-up for Breakthrough of the Year, on 22 December 2016.

entries.title: Bob Dylan wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
entries.subtitle: Songwriting receives a literary distinction
entries.summary: Bob Dylan's 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature recognised poetry created through song. The choice drew attention to the relationship between words, voice and music within an award often associated with writing for the page.
body: The Swedish Academy named Bob Dylan its Nobel Prize in Literature laureate on 13 October 2016, recognising his renewal of poetic expression within the American song tradition. The award honoured work shaped through words, voice and music. By choosing a songwriter for a distinction commonly associated with novels, plays and printed poetry, the Academy brought the literary possibilities of performed song into view.

entries.title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
entries.subtitle: Newt Scamander's suitcase opens in New York
entries.summary: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them follows a researcher carrying magical creatures through 1926 New York. When they escape, his effort to care for them draws an unsuspecting baker into the wizarding world's rules and dangers.
body: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them takes the wizarding world to New York in 1926. Eddie Redmayne plays Newt Scamander, a researcher carrying creatures gathered on his travels inside a suitcase. David Yates directed the film, which marked J.K. Rowling's screenwriting debut. It opened in France on 16 November 2016, followed by Britain and the United States on 18 November.

A suitcase mix-up brings Newt into contact with Jacob Kowalski, a baker who knows nothing about magic. Creatures escape into the city, and searching for them draws the two men into the lives of Tina and Queenie Goldstein. Newt must navigate unfamiliar streets and rules enforced by the American magical authorities. When Jacob enters the much larger world inside the suitcase, his first encounter with its habitats and inhabitants becomes a way for the audience to discover them too.

Newt's work depends on observing each creature's behaviour and needs. That changes the pace of the chases and encounters: a small animal drawn to valuables calls for a different response from a frightened or powerful creature. Alongside this care, a wider danger develops in the city, bringing concealment and persecution into the story. James Newton Howard's score gives the film a new musical identity. The production also reunites Yates with Harry Potter colleagues, including designer Stuart Craig and producer David Heyman.

story_headings: Jyn Erso and the Death Star plans
A war story before A New Hope
body: Rogue One follows Jyn Erso, a woman whose father has been drawn into the Empire’s weapons programme. Rebel intelligence officer Cassian Andor brings her into a mission connected to the Death Star. Their companions come from different corners of the conflict, joining an effort to obtain the battle station’s plans before the Empire can consolidate its power.

Gareth Edwards directs this 2016 film, set immediately before A New Hope. It develops an event already central to the first film through the people sent to carry it out. Michael Giacchino’s score accompanies a story focused on intelligence work, occupation and a military operation, expanding the saga through another group’s role in the Rebellion.

entries.title: MeToo movement
entries.summary: The #MeToo hashtag spread widely in October 2017, bringing survivors' experiences of harassment and assault into public view. Tarana Burke's earlier language of empathy and solidarity became part of an international discussion about abuse and power.
body: The #MeToo hashtag gained wide attention in October 2017 after reports of sexual-abuse allegations against producer Harvey Weinstein. Survivors shared experiences of harassment and assault, showing how widespread they were. Activist Tarana Burke had used the phrase in this context around 2006, with an emphasis on empathy and solidarity. On 15 October 2017, actress Alyssa Milano encouraged women to post the words on social media. The ensuing testimony connected individual accounts in a collective discussion, bringing workplace abuse and the power that enabled it to the centre of public attention.
story_headings: A phrase connects survivors' experiences

provenance.date_note: The movement's global expansion after the Weinstein reporting. Verified source identifies this subject and milestone in2017. Day retained only when explicitly supported; no festival premiere substituted for a stated theatrical-release milestone.
provenance.full_source_extract:
#MeToo is a social movement and awareness campaign against sexual abuse, sexual harassment, and rape culture, in which survivors (led by the voices of women, especially public figures) share their experiences of sexual abuse or sexual harassment. The phrase "Me Too" was initially used in this context on social media around 2006, on Myspace, by sexual assault survivor and activist Tarana Burke. The hashtag #MeToo was used starting in 2017 as a way to draw attention to the magnitude of the problem. "Me Too" is meant to empower those who have been sexually assaulted through empathy, solidarity and strength in numbers, by visibly demonstrating how many have experienced sexual assault and harassment, especially in the workplace.
Following multiple exposures of sexual-abuse allegations against film producer Harvey Weinstein in October 2017, the movement began to spread virally as a hashtag on social media. On October 15, 2017, American actress Alyssa Milano posted on Twitter encouraging women to use the phrase "Me Too" in their social media posts to demonstrate the widespread prevalence of sexual harassment and assault, stating that the idea came from a friend. A number of high-profile posts and responses from American celebrities Gwyneth Paltrow, Ashley Judd, Jennifer Lawrence, and Uma Thurman, among others, soon followed. Widespread media coverage and discussion of sexual harassment, particularly in Hollywood, led to high-profile terminations from positions held, as well as criticism and backlash.
After millions of people started using the phrase and hashtag in this manner in English, the expression began to spread to dozens of other languages. The scope has become somewhat broader with this expansion, however, and Burke has more recently referred to it as an international movement for justice for marginalized people. After the hashtag #MeToo went viral in late 2017, Facebook reported that almost half of its American users were friends with someone who said they had been sexually assaulted or harassed.
The #MeToo movement has sparked debate over how to support survivors while ensuring due process for the accused. Although some worry about false accusations and premature consequences, studies by the United States Department of Justice and UK Home Office estimate that false reports make up only 2–10% of sexual assault claims. Commentators like Jude Doyle and Jennifer Wright argue that #BelieveWomen is not a call to abandon due process but a response to the rarity of false allegations. Critics also highlight gaps in the movement’s reach, including its failure to address police abuse, include sex workers, or center marginalized women, who face the highest rates of violence.

entries.title: Star Wars: Episode VIII – The Last Jedi
entries.summary: Rey asks Luke Skywalker for help as Leia’s Resistance flees the First Order. The search for a teacher unfolds alongside a fleet’s struggle to survive.
story_headings: Rey seeks Luke while the Resistance flees
Passing on the Jedi legacy
body: The Last Jedi follows Rey to the isolated planet Ahch-To, where she hopes to bring Luke Skywalker back to the Resistance. The First Order continues its pursuit of Leia’s depleted forces. Finn and the mechanic Rose undertake another mission to help the fleet escape, while Rey’s encounter with Luke forces both to confront the legacy of the Jedi.

Rian Johnson writes and directs the 2017 middle chapter of the sequel trilogy. Luke’s experience gives Rey’s search for a teacher a different starting point from his own youthful training. The film moves between their conversations and the fleet’s diminishing options, connecting questions about the past to the immediate survival of the Resistance. John Williams returns as composer.

The beginnings of a familiar partnership
body: Solo follows the young Han Solo before he meets Luke and Leia. Trying to make a life beyond the control of others, he enters a dangerous criminal world and joins a crew undertaking risky jobs. The journey brings him to Chewbacca and the gambler Lando Calrissian, connecting his early ambitions to the companions and ship known from later films.

Ron Howard directs the 2018 adventure, with Alden Ehrenreich playing Han and Donald Glover playing Lando. Heists and shifting loyalties give the film its structure within the period of Imperial rule. John Powell composes the score, while John Williams supplies a new Han Solo theme, linking the character’s younger life to the saga’s orchestral tradition.

entries.title: General Data Protection Regulation
entries.summary: The General Data Protection Regulation sets rules for handling personal information in the EU and European Economic Area. Applicable in the EU from May 2018, it strengthens individual rights while seeking to simplify the rules for international business.
body:
The General Data Protection Regulation, or GDPR, is the EU's Regulation 2016/679 on personal information. It forms part of the privacy and human-rights framework associated with Article 8(1) of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. Its scope covers the EU and European Economic Area, including rules on transferring personal data outside them. The aim is to give people greater control and stronger rights over their information while simplifying rules and terminology for businesses operating internationally. It replaces Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC.

The European Parliament approved the reform on 14 April 2016; the final regulation of Parliament and the Council is dated 27 April. It entered into force on 24 May 2016 and began applying in the EU on 25 May 2018. As a regulation, it applies directly without needing to be transposed into national law. It nevertheless leaves member states room for specific national rules and exceptions within the limits it sets.
story_headings: Individual rights and common rules

provenance.full_source_extract:
The General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), abbreviated GDPR, is a European Union regulation on information privacy in the European Union (EU) and the European Economic Area (EEA). The GDPR is an important component of EU privacy law and human rights law, in particular Article 8(1) of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. It also governs the transfer of personal data outside the EU and EEA. The GDPR's goals are to enhance individuals' control and rights over their personal information and to simplify the regulations for international business. It supersedes the Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC and, among other things, simplifies the terminology.
The European Parliament and Council of the European Union adopted the GDPR on 14 April 2016, to become effective on 25 May 2018. As an EU regulation (instead of a directive), the GDPR has direct legal effect and does not require transposition into national law. However, it also provides flexibility for individual member states to modify (derogate from) some of its provisions.
As an example of the Brussels effect, the regulation became a model for many other laws around the world, including in Brazil, Japan, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Thailand. After leaving the European Union, the United Kingdom enacted its "UK GDPR", identical to the GDPR. The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), adopted on 28 June 2018, has many similarities with the GDPR.

entries.subtitle: Newt faces a struggle over the magical world's future
entries.summary: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald draws Newt Scamander into a struggle for power within the wizarding world. A search through Paris brings personal loyalties and family histories into conflict as Grindelwald gathers followers.
body: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald expands Newt Scamander's travels into a conflict over power within the wizarding world. David Yates returns to direct, with J.K. Rowling again writing the screenplay. The sequel introduces Jude Law as a younger Albus Dumbledore. It opened in France on 14 November 2018, followed by Britain and the United States on 16 November.

Dumbledore asks his former pupil Newt to help oppose Gellert Grindelwald, played by Johnny Depp. The search leads to Paris, where Newt, Tina, Jacob and Queenie encounter people seeking answers about Credence. Newt's brother Theseus and Leta Lestrange bring their own history into the journey. Moving between these characters makes their personal relationships part of the struggle for power, as old loyalties complicate the decisions they must now make.

Grindelwald wins support by describing a future that gives his listeners reasons to overlook the violence behind his movement. As it grows, Newt finds it harder to maintain his distance from the competing institutions. The creatures still play a part in the action, but discovering them now sits alongside questions of allegiance and family history. James Newton Howard returns as composer, adding new themes and the title track to the musical material established in the first film.

entries.title: Fridays for Future
entries.summary: Fridays for Future brings school students into demonstrations demanding action on climate change and a transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy. Greta Thunberg's 2018 protest outside Sweden's parliament helped prompt international organising and global strikes in 2019.
body:
Fridays for Future, often shortened to FFF and also called the School Strike for Climate, is an international student movement. Participants miss Friday classes to demand that political leaders act on climate change and that the fossil-fuel industry move towards renewable energy. The movement gained attention after Swedish pupil Greta Thunberg began protesting outside the Riksdag in August 2018. Her sign read Skolstrejk för klimatet: school strike for the climate.

On 15 March 2019, a global strike brought together more than a million participants at 2,200 events in 125 countries. A second global strike on 24 May drew hundreds of thousands to 1,600 protests across 150 countries. Its timing coincided with the 2019 European Parliament election, linking the demonstrations to a moment when voters were choosing representatives.
story_headings: From a sign outside parliament to global strikes

provenance.full_source_extract:
Fridays for Future (FFF), also known as the School Strike for Climate (Swedish: Skolstrejk för klimatet [ˈskûːlstrɛjk fœr klɪˈmɑ̌ːtɛt]), is an international movement of school students who skip Friday classes to participate in demonstrations to demand action from political leaders to prevent climate change and for the fossil fuel industry to transition to renewable energy. Publicity and widespread organising began after Swedish pupil Greta Thunberg staged a protest in August 2018 outside of the Swedish parliament, the Riksdag, holding a sign that read "Skolstrejk för klimatet" ("School strike for the climate").
A global strike on 15 March 2019 gathered more than one million strikers in 2,200 strikes organised in 125 countries. On 24 May 2019, in the second global strike, 1,600 protests across 150 countries drew hundreds of thousands of strikers. The May protests were timed to coincide with the 2019 European Parliament election.
The 2019 Global Week for Future was a series of 4,500 strikes across over 150 countries, focused around Friday 20 September and Friday 27 September. Likely the largest climate strikes in world history, the 20 September strikes gathered roughly 4 million protesters, many of them schoolchildren, including 1.4 million in Germany. On 27 September, an estimated two million people participated in demonstrations worldwide, including over one million protesters in Italy and several hundred thousand protesters in Canada.

entries.title: The first image of a black hole
entries.summary: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration revealed an image of the black hole in Messier 87 in April 2019. Combining radio observations from around the world made it possible to distinguish a bright ring surrounding its dark shadow.
body:
On 10 April 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration revealed the first image of a black hole. A bright ring surrounded the dark shadow of the supermassive black hole in Messier 87, about fifty-five million light-years from Earth.

The team combined observations from radio telescopes around the world to form a virtual instrument the size of Earth. Years of international collaboration and technical development made that combination possible. Its resolving power allowed the researchers to study structures close to a black hole's event horizon.
story_headings: An Earth-sized instrument reveals a shadow

provenance.date_note: Publication of the first image of a black hole. Verified source identifies this subject and milestone in2019. Day retained only when explicitly supported; no festival premiere substituted for a stated theatrical-release milestone.
provenance.full_source_extract:
The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) is a telescope array consisting of a global network of radio telescopes. The EHT project combines data from several very-long-baseline interferometry (VLBI) stations around Earth, which form a combined array with an angular resolution sufficient to observe objects the size of a supermassive black hole's event horizon. The project's observational targets include the two black holes with the largest angular diameter as observed from Earth: the black hole at the center of the supergiant elliptical galaxy Messier 87, and Sagittarius A*, at the center of the Milky Way.
The Event Horizon Telescope project is an international collaboration that was launched in 2009 after a long period of theoretical and technical developments. On the theory side, work on the photon orbit and first simulations of what a black hole would look like progressed to predictions of VLBI imaging for the Galactic Center black hole, Sgr A*. Technical advances in radio observing moved from the first detection of Sgr A*, through VLBI at progressively shorter wavelengths, ultimately leading to detection of horizon scale structure in both Sgr A* and M87. The collaboration now comprises over 300 members, and 60 institutions, working in over 20 countries and regions.
The first image of a black hole, at the center of galaxy Messier 87, was published by the EHT Collaboration on April 10, 2019, in a series of six scientific publications. The array made this observation at a wavelength of 1.3 mm and with a theoretical diffraction-limited resolution of 25 microarcseconds. In March 2021, the Collaboration presented, for the first time, a polarized-based image of the black hole which may help better reveal the forces giving rise to quasars. Future plans involve improving the array's resolution by adding new telescopes and by taking shorter-wavelength observations. On 12 May 2022, astronomers unveiled the first image of the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A*.
Since 2018 the EHT has been capable of imaging at a wavelength of 870 μm (345 GHz), giving an angular resolution of 19 μas, the best resolution of any ground-based telescope.

entries.title: Avengers: Endgame
entries.summary: Avengers: Endgame is a 2019 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo.
body: Avengers: Endgame is a 2019 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo. It follows the survivors of Avengers: Infinity War after the villain Thanos has erased half of all life. Tony Stark (Iron Man), Steve Rogers (Captain America), Natasha Romanoff (Black Widow) and their remaining allies must decide whether anything can be done to reverse that loss. The film first gives space to grief and changed relationships, establishing why another mission matters before bringing the team back into action.

Released in United States cinemas on 26 April 2019, Endgame draws together storylines developed across the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Its return to earlier moments allows familiar places and encounters to take on different meanings for characters who have lived through the intervening events. Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans and Scarlett Johansson return alongside the ensemble cast. Alan Silvestri’s orchestral score connects the large action sequences to the personal decisions that conclude this part of the Avengers’ shared story.

entries.title: Chernobyl
entries.subtitle: Understanding an accident while trying to contain it
entries.summary: Chernobyl dramatises the 1986 nuclear accident through the people investigating its causes and limiting its damage. The five-part HBO/Sky series follows how technical knowledge, official decisions and emergency work shape one another as the disaster unfolds.
body: Chernobyl follows the people investigating the 1986 nuclear accident and trying to contain its damage. Written by Craig Mazin and directed by Johan Renck, the five-part HBO/Sky miniseries began on HBO in the United States on 6 May 2019. Jared Harris, Stellan Skarsgård and Emily Watson lead a story that moves between technical decisions, official explanations and the human cost of emergency work.

The opening episodes stay close to the confusion and physical work around the reactor. Firefighters, plant staff and medical workers face a danger that ordinary experience does not always help them recognise. Scientific knowledge becomes useful when it changes an order or a procedure, bringing its bearers into conflict with officials seeking reassurance and control over the account of events. The drama follows the gap between those who have enough information to understand a risk and those sent to face it.

Later episodes connect the emergency response with the investigation into the accident. Mazin builds technical explanations around decisions: as the characters come to understand the reactor differently, their view of responsibility also changes. Filmed in Lithuania, the production uses its locations to give the work both industrial and domestic settings. Renck's measured pacing lets an evacuation, a shift or an instruction acquire weight before its consequences become fully clear.

Working before the danger is understood

entries.summary: Bong Joon Ho's Parasite follows a poor family entering the home and lives of a wealthy household. The film combines black comedy and suspense around that unequal relationship, reaching audiences worldwide after its recognition at Cannes.
body: Parasite premiered at Cannes on 21 May 2019 and became the first Korean film to win the Palme d'Or. Bong Joon Ho's story follows a poor family gradually entering the home and lives of a wealthy household. He initially imagined it as a play, but the project developed into a film, with Han Jin-won co-writing the screenplay. Black comedy and thriller elements grow out of the families' unequal relationship. Released in South Korea on 30 May 2019, Parasite found an international audience, earning about 258 million dollars against a production budget of 11.4 million.

provenance.full_source_extract:
Parasite (Korean: 기생충) is a 2019 South Korean black comedy thriller film directed by Bong Joon Ho, who co-wrote the screenplay with Han Jin-won. It stars Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong, Choi Woo-shik, Park So-dam, Jang Hye-jin, Park Myung-hoon, and Lee Jung-eun. The film follows a poor family who infiltrate the home and life of a wealthy family.
The script is based on a play Bong wrote in 2013. He later adapted it into a 15-page film draft, which was split into three different drafts by Han. Bong said he was inspired by the Korean film The Housemaid (1960) and the 1930s Christine and Léa Papin incident. Filming ran from May to September 2018 and included cinematographer Hong Kyung-pyo, editor Yang Jin-mo, and composer Jung Jae-il. Parasite premiered on 21 May 2019 at the Cannes Film Festival, where it became the first Korean film to win the Palme d'Or. It was praised for its direction, screenplay, performances, editing, and production design. It was released in South Korea by CJ Entertainment on 30 May, grossing $258 million worldwide on an $11.4 million budget.
Among its numerous accolades, Parasite won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 92nd Academy Awards, becoming the first non-English-language film to do so. It won an additional three Oscars, for Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, and Best International Feature Film. It is the first South Korean film to receive any Academy Award recognition, and one of only four films overall to win both the Palme d'Or and the Academy Award for Best Picture, the first such achievement in over 60 years. It won the Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language and the BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language, and became the first non-English-language film to win the Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture. 
Since its release, Parasite has been regarded as Bong's magnum opus and was ranked in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll as the 90th best film of all time. In 2025, The New York Times ranked it as the best movie of the 21st century so far in a list based on a vote by readers, actors, and directors. As of February 2025, an HBO limited television series based on the film is in early development.

entries.title: Joker
entries.subtitle: Arthur Fleck searches for an audience
entries.summary: Todd Phillips' Joker follows a Gotham clown who hopes to become a stand-up comedian. Joaquin Phoenix's movements, strained laughter and discomfort give physical form to Arthur Fleck's search for recognition and his increasingly violent actions.
body: Joker centres on Arthur Fleck, a struggling Gotham clown who hopes to become a stand-up comedian. Directed by Todd Phillips, the film makes Joaquin Phoenix's movements, strained laughter and discomfort central to its account of Arthur. It premiered in Venice on 31 August 2019 and opened in the United States on 4 October, offering a new origin for Batman's familiar adversary.

Arthur's work and ambitions repeatedly bring him before people who dismiss or humiliate him. His attachment to a television host provides an imagined audience before he has a real one. Phillips and co-writer Scott Silver stay close to Arthur's experience, allowing wishful thinking to enter scenes that initially seem ordinary. As his actions become more violent, the attention they attract gives them a public meaning that extends beyond the man who committed them.

Hildur Guðnadóttir began composing from the screenplay before filming started. Her cello-led score places Arthur's unease beneath the images, and music already written for the production helped shape Phoenix's bathroom dance. A private physical gesture becomes a moment of transformation. Through this partnership between music and performance, Arthur's body can express a change before he explains it. Joker received the Golden Lion at Venice.

The audience Arthur imagines
A score that shapes a dance

story_headings: Rey and her friends face the last confrontation
Closing the nine-film Skywalker story
body: The Rise of Skywalker reunites Rey, Finn and Poe Dameron as the Resistance faces a renewed threat. A message associated with Emperor Palpatine draws the conflict back toward the Sith, while Rey continues to develop her command of the Force. Her connection to Kylo Ren remains tied to the choices ahead, bringing personal questions into the wider struggle.

J.J. Abrams returns to direct the 2019 conclusion of the sequel trilogy and the nine-film Skywalker saga. The group’s journey draws together characters and conflicts introduced across the three trilogies. John Williams also returns to the score, combining familiar themes with new music as the film closes the storyline begun with the original Star Wars in 1977.

entries.title: COVID-19 pandemic
entries.summary: COVID-19 spread worldwide in early 2020 after an outbreak identified in Wuhan the previous December. The response developed through emergency measures and vaccination programmes, while changing variants affected transmission and the threat continued beyond the formal international emergency.
body:
COVID-19 spread around the world in early 2020 after an outbreak identified in Wuhan in December 2019. The World Health Organization declared an international health emergency on 30 January 2020 and characterised the outbreak as a pandemic on 11 March. Airborne transmission helped the virus spread, while new variants changed patterns of infection.

Vaccines were developed rapidly. Large-scale vaccination campaigns began in December 2020, with national and international programmes extending their reach. On 5 May 2023, WHO ended the international health emergency while continuing to recognise COVID-19 as a global health threat. The end of that emergency status therefore did not mean the disappearance of the disease.
story_headings: Emergency declarations and the vaccination response

provenance.date_note: The World Health Organization characterises COVID-19 as a pandemic.
provenance.full_source_extract:
The global COVID-19 pandemic (also known as the coronavirus pandemic), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. It spread to other parts of Asia and then worldwide in early 2020. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on 30 January 2020 and assessed it as having become a pandemic on 11 March. The WHO declared that the public health emergency caused by COVID-19 had ended in May 2023, while noting that COVID-19 continued to be a global health threat.
COVID-19 symptoms range from asymptomatic to deadly, but most commonly include fever, sore throat, nocturnal cough, and fatigue. Transmission of the virus is often through airborne particles. Mutations have produced many strains (variants) with varying degrees of infectivity and virulence. COVID-19 vaccines were developed rapidly and deployed to the general public beginning in December 2020, made available through government and international programmes such as COVAX, aiming to provide vaccine equity. Treatments include novel antiviral drugs and symptom control. Common mitigation measures during the public health emergency included travel restrictions, lockdowns, business restrictions and closures, workplace hazard controls, mask mandates, quarantines, testing systems, and contact tracing of the infected.
The pandemic caused severe social and economic disruption around the world, including the largest global recession since the Great Depression. Widespread supply shortages, including food shortages, were caused by supply chain disruptions and panic buying. Reduced human activity led to an unprecedented temporary decrease in pollution. Educational institutions and public areas were partially or fully closed in many jurisdictions, and many events were cancelled or postponed during 2020 and 2021. Telework became much more common for white-collar workers as the pandemic evolved. Misinformation circulated through social media and occasionally through mass media, and political tensions intensified. The pandemic raised issues of racial and geographic discrimination, health equity, and the balance between public health imperatives and individual rights.
The disease has continued to circulate since 2023. By 2025, experts generally believed the pandemic to be over, having transitioned into the endemic phase. Different definitions of pandemics lead to different determinations of when they end. As of 18 September 2026, COVID-19 has caused 7,115,706 confirmed deaths and 18.5 to 35.2 million estimated deaths.

entries.title: George Floyd protests
entries.summary: Protests against police brutality began in Minneapolis on 26 May 2020 after George Floyd's murder during an arrest. Bystander video and accounts of his death spread, drawing demonstrations across the United States and beyond.
body:
Demonstrations against police brutality began in Minneapolis on 26 May 2020 following the murder of George Floyd, an unarmed forty-six-year-old African American man, during an arrest. Veteran officer Derek Chauvin kept his knee on Floyd's neck for nine minutes and twenty-nine seconds as Floyd said he could not breathe. Two other officers helped restrain him while a fourth kept bystanders back. All four were dismissed and later arrested.

Video recorded by a bystander and word of mouth spread within hours of the killing. Protesters gathered at East 38th Street and Chicago Avenue, where Floyd had been arrested and killed, and elsewhere in the Minneapolis–Saint Paul area. Demonstrations and unrest then spread nationally and internationally. In April 2021, a jury found Chauvin guilty of second-degree murder, third-degree murder and second-degree manslaughter. In June, he received a state prison sentence of twenty-two and a half years.
story_headings: The killing, the protests and the state verdict

images.title: George Floyd protesters, 2020
images.creator: Dan Aasland
